articles.title: You can now order the new Nintendo 64 and Sega Genesis controllers for Switch
articles.summary: Nintendo has launched purchase pages for its new Nintendo 64 and Sega Genesis controllers that can work with games being added to its Nintendo Switch Online service. They’re $49.99 each.
articles.body: To faithfully play the Nintendo 64 and Sega Genesis games coming to Nintendo Switch Online, you’re going to want the original controllers. Nintendo has posted pages for both the revised Nintendo 64 and Genesis controllers, and you can buy one right now if you’re a Nintendo Switch Online subscriber. Each one costs $49.99 and includes USB-C charging. In the case of the N64 controller, it includes built-in rumble for games that support it, like Star Fox 64. Both controllers are set to ship on October 25th, and Nintendo is limiting account holders to four of each. Nintendo Switch Online is the paid service that nets you cloud save backups and access to Tetris 99, retro SNES and NES games, and other content. The cost of that membership is going to go up for people who want access to N64 and Genesis games. My colleague Chaim Gartenberg has all of the pricing details for you here. Though, you don’t need to purchase these controllers to be able to play the new games being added to the plan.

articles.title: BMW iX3 first drive: a ‘New Class’ is in session
articles.summary: BMW’s iX3, the automaker’s first Neue Klasse vehicle, is a game changer in its first drive experience.
articles.body: BMW has been peppering us with teasers and bits and pieces about its next-gen EV platform, Neue Klasse, for so long — fully two years now — that I confess I’ve become a bit numb to the hype. I’d seen the dashboard-filling displays, talked to engineers endlessly about the completely retooled active safety suite, and even got a go behind the wheel of a prototype machine. All this for the launch of a crossover SUV, typically the most milquetoast of all the automotive classifications. But after spending the better part of a day wheeling around the final version of the iX3, I’m surprised to say it was all worth it. This little(ish) SUV really is a game changer on multiple fronts, a major step forward for BMW’s electric efforts, and a machine that might even be good enough to beat the EV sales slump. Platform basics For carmakers, platforms are key. They’re the core elements that allow relatively quick and inexpensive development of multiple new models without having to completely reinvent core elements like chassis, engines, suspension, and software. Neue Klasse (German for “New Class”) is BMW’s latest and greatest new platform, intended to form the foundation of a series of EVs to come. The iX3 is the first of those, a compact SUV that’s more or less the same size as BMW’s existing X3, offering similar amounts of cargo and space for five passengers. This new platform tucks the battery down low and pushes its two motors to the front and rear. None of that is novel in the EV space, but most of BMW’s previous EVs have relied on platforms designed for internal combustion. This one’s optimized for EVs from the beginning. There’s a 108.7kWh usable battery pack in there, powering the pair of motors that, combined, offer 463 horsepower and 476 pound-feet of torque through all four wheels. Maximum range will be around 400 miles (EPA testing has not yet been completed), 40-odd more than Tesla’s longest-range Model Y. BMW’s engineers told me that the iX3’s new electrical architecture is really the key, including more efficient motors and silicon-carbide inverters. It charges faster, too, at up to 400kW if you can find a plug backed by enough juice. That’ll be a NACS plug, by the way, as this will be BMW’s first to support the Tesla-style connector. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: Tech boost A quick glance in the cabin of the iX3 reveals the SUV’s biggest tech upgrade: the pillar-to-pillar Panoramic Vision display. Think of it like an ultra-widescreen heads-up display that acts as a gauge cluster on the left, but has six customizable sections in the middle and the right where you can display anything from efficiency information to whatever’s playing on Spotify. Enough never being enough, the iX3 also has an actual 3D heads-up display that projects above the Panoramic Vision, plus a 17.9-inch, 3,340 x 1,440 rhomboid-shaped touchscreen for good measure. It’s display overload and a little overwhelming the first time you get in the car, but I found it to be seamless enough to not be a distraction. If it all seems like a bit too much for you, it’s easy enough to disable the more expansive or attention-grabbing display sections. The in-car experience is paired with an upgraded My BMW app that not only lets you remotely park the car from outside and get a 3D view of the inside or outside of the car; you can even queue up playlists on your phone or give your passengers control to do the same from their own devices. To experience the more important tech upgrades, though, you need to be behind the wheel. Next-gen active safety Taking back control from many of today’s more advanced active safety systems in cars can sometimes feel like wrestling. Often, a firm yank of the wheel is required to override a lane-centering system, which can result in a disconcertingly jerky experience for your passengers. The iX3, on the other hand, is designed to be totally seamless. If you have BMW’s Highway Assistant enabled, it’ll steer itself in most situations on the highway, but you can just reach up and grab the wheel whenever you like. There’s no resistance to overcome, and if you let go the car just takes over again. Even if you want to change lanes the car can help you there. When prompted, glance in the mirror and the car will change lanes on its own. Or, if you grab the wheel and change lanes yourself, the car will apply the turn signal for you automatically. BMW’s system will also stay enabled if you hit the brake pedal. You can come to a complete stop if you like, then release the brake and the car will smoothly bring itself back up to speed. The system stays engaged until you turn it off — or hit the brakes more aggressively — working with you instead of against you. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: The drive experience This new safety system feels a bit odd at first. It took me some time to figure out when it was on and when it was off. But, after a few minutes on the highway, I got into the groove of things. It really did feel more like working collaboratively with the car instead of having its systems constantly turning on and off. The hands-off system worked extremely well, too, cleanly moving through traffic. It wasn’t until I hit some secondary country roads that I could get a feel for just how good the iX3 was to drive, though. That dual-motor setup means full-time all-wheel drive, but the power split between those two motors changes depending on what drive mode you’re in. The car feels safe and secure in Personal, the regular drive mode. Drive it as aggressively as you want and it just has a calm, predictable nature that makes it easy to keep pointed in the right direction without too much input from the driver. Switch over to Sport, though, and the tail kicks out just a bit under hard acceleration, making the iX3 feel like a traditional, rear-driven BMW. This isn’t a rocket ship, but it is quick and the suspension strikes a great balance between predictable, comfortable handling and sporty response. Even the steering feels sharp and has respectable feedback, just like BMWs of old. In a lot of ways, this wholly new package feels like a return to form, a new SUV that has engaging driving and safety at its core but blends in enough luxury and refinement to keep its premium cachet. But it isn’t a sure-fire success. For one thing, there’s the look. BMW has been pushing boundaries with many of its latest designs, and the iX3 certainly has an edgy style. After initially hating it, I have to admit that after a day behind the wheel I quickly warmed up to the iX3’s appearance, particularly when viewed from the rear. Even if you like the SUV’s style, there’s still the question of cost. BMW hasn’t set formal pricing for the 2026 BMW iX3 yet, only that it will start around $60,000. That puts it at least $10,000 more than a base, gas-powered X3 SUV. With federal EV incentives no longer at play, that delta could be a difficult one for many shoppers to stomach. But, despite sharing most of a name, these two SUVs feel worlds apart. With enough range and fast enough charging to obliterate range anxiety, plus with an abundance of volume, handling, and comfort, the EV is the obvious play for those with room in their budget. Photography by Tim Stevens

articles.title: TOEM 2 Is Charming Sequel That Once Again Uses Its Novel In-game Camera As a Lens to Solve Neat Puzzles and Explore Its Monochrome World - Review
articles.summary: The novelty has worn off a smidge, but this sequel is still great on its own terms.
articles.body:
When a troll blocking a bridge wants a photo of three goats, you get him a photo of three goats. Not only must you find goats to photograph, but you must perfectly position these goats – on three different ledges – to get all three in the photograph. TOEM 2 is full of these sorts of environmental puzzles that cleverly use a photo mode mechanic through the lens of your own in-game camera to define its gameplay. It is a hidden object game insomuch as you're searching for hidden objects, but it's no June's Journey, where you're searching through static images to pick out items. TOEM 2's world, like the original, is dynamic, surprising, and an absolute delight.

As the title would suggest, TOEM 2 is the follow-up to TOEM: A Photo Adventure from developer Something We Made, which was released in 2021. TOEM 2 is exceptionally similar to TOEM; the foundation remains exactly the same. You control a young lad who heads out from their quaint home to see an awe-inspiring seasonal event called the toem. Playing as that little guy, you travel from your home through three distinct towns in monochrome isometry. Bus tickets are necessary to keep moving from town to town, and those are earned through helping townsfolk. And to help these townsfolk is to take photos.

You'll take photos of all sorts of things: Hidden garden gnomes, stinky cheese, and cute little critters. Each town in TOEM 2 is a series of connected, isometric dioramas rendered in a soft, 3D style and only in shades of black and white. The townsfolk retain the flatter, more hand-drawn aesthetic from the first game, letting them stand out among the environment. Creatures skitter about, clouds linger in the sky. Along the way, an invisible man on one forest block of the town may need a potion to become visible again (he’s only visible through the camera lens). A potion maker resides several blocks away; once you stumble upon him, he’ll ask for toadstools, send you out once again. Only then you’ll be able to make your way back to the invisible man and hand over the potion. Most of TOEM 2’s objectives typically play out like this and work as a way to encourage further exploration of the world. A lot of the time, you’ll find something surprising, or silly – a cat hiding in a flower pot, perhaps – and snap a photo. It’s so curious that it probably means something, but you’ve just not figured that out yet.

Beyond taking photos, each of these towns has a little gimmick tied to the camera. In the quaint farmland town Cropten, vines are spreading, blocking entrances and pathways. One of the first townspeople you’ll meet will attach a pair of scissors to your camera. That first townsperson, in Cropten, is a little worm who's very concerned about the vines. Instead of point-and-shoot, it’s also now point-and-snip. Vines pop up every now and then, the little worm would panic, and I'd gladly take care of it for them. The two other towns, Taletorp and Deltburg, have their own respective tools and enjoyable little, ongoing storyline around using them. And you can't miss the charming townsfolk you're introduced to immediately at the start of each level; they serve to tutorialize your new tools, and become a friend to wander about with.

TOEM 2 is about four or five hours long, so its simple premise never feels like a chore. Each of the worlds are so individually delightful that I didn't want to rush through any one location. It's one of the very rare games in which I was eager to seek out everything there was to discover. There are many more puzzles to solve than there are bus tickets required to progress, and once you've collected those bus tickets, the only incentive for continuing is the sheer joy of seeking what happens. There is a scarecrow, for instance, that wants to see the world and you can snap him in-and-out of different locations: at much too high heights, near a cozy fireplace, or back with some pesky birds. It's the three hidden gnomes that I've got in the back of my mind throughout it, checking nooks and crannies to see if I can spot them. Joy, throughout TOEM 2, is hopping off objects and onto rooftops, navigating curving platforms to reach the farthest peaks just to gain a new perspective on the world.

Oddly, TOEM 2's biggest limitation is that the original TOEM is fantastic. Using a camera to engage with the world through a neat photo mode in its particular way felt exceptionally novel; TOEM 2's camera upgrades and tools don't necessarily elevate it beyond that level of uniqueness. TOEM's art is hand-drawn, in a way that feels more intimate and raw; While TOEM 2 ' s characters retain that style, the world and its items are computer-modeled. It's still lovely and well-crafted, but it doesn't feel like an improvement or expansion on the first game.

Most prominently, though, TOEM's puzzles were a bit more engaging. TOEM 2 is very gentle, and effortlessly guides you through its photographic treasure hunt. It was breezy to play, and although that's not necessarily a bad thing, the touch of friction in the first game encouraged a deeper degree of curiosity. For instance, TOEM 2 has a quality-of-life sort of update to its camera – being able to lock the camera onto an object makes it much easier to capture photos of fast-moving objects, like a paper plane gliding in the air. It's a seemingly insignificant change that removes that stroke of friction that I wish TOEM 2 had. It wasn't exactly difficult to take photos without the focus lock, but it meant putting in some work for your perfect picture.

When answering the question of 'What does this all lead to?,' the end of TOEM 2 may seem disappointing. The toem phenomenon that the game is centered around isn't all too different from that of the first game. But TOEM 2 isn't disappointing on the whole, because it was never at all about reaching the end. Forgive me, but it really is what you've seen and discovered along the way.

articles.title: Star Wars Tabletop Games Are Discounted For Prime Day, Including Unlimited
articles.summary: Save on Star Wars Unlimited, The Deckbuilding Game, and Outer Rim with these Prime Day deals at Amazon
articles.body:
Star Wars is a universe ripe for adventure, intrigue, memorable characters, and… merchandise. George Lucas’ decades-spanning franchise has given us millions of toys, clothes, and just about anything else you can think of, and there are also a whole host of tabletop experiences for your next game night.

We’ve dug through this October’s Prime Day deals to find some excellent options to play with friends and family - here are our picks.

Save On Star Wars Card Games and More This Prime Day

Kicking things off, we’ve got Star Wars: The Deckbuilding Game from Fantasy Flight Games (more on them shortly).

This head-to-head card game offers a chance to play as the Galactic Empire or the Rebel Alliance, each with its own playstyle and card choices as you look to destroy your opponents’ bases before they destroy yours.

There are over 50 different cards and iconic bases, with matches taking around 30 minutes. Whether you’re recruiting Luke Skywalker or Darth Vader, the game is reduced by 15%, bringing it from $33.59 to $28.49 .

Star Wars: Unlimited Shadows of the Galaxy Starter Set

Sticking with Fantasy Flight Games, the company is now best known for Star Wars: Unlimited, the popular trading card game.

It’s a really fun game that offers both space and ground battles simultaneously, and one Prime Day deal makes it cheaper to learn.

The Star Wars: Unlimited Shadows of the Galaxy Starter Set , which includes themed decks for The Mandalorian and Moff Gideon, is a hair short of being half price. It’s dropped from $34.99 down to $17.99, which is a new lowest-ever price.

Finally, Star Wars: Outer Rim from—you guessed it—Fantasy Flight Games is a three-to-four-hour game that has you playing as a bounty hunter like Han Solo, IG-88, or Boba Fett.

There’s a whole host of pieces in the box if you’re into that sort of thing, and with modular boards, every playthrough feels unique.

It’s currently $61.49, a 28% discount on the $84.99 MSRP , although we have seen it cheaper. Still, if you’re looking for a fun game to play with friends, this is worth a look - and this price will only last for a few hours.

Lloyd Coombes is an experienced freelancer in tech, gaming and fitness seen at Polygon, Eurogamer, Macworld, TechRadar and many more. He's a big fan of Magic: The Gathering and other collectible card games, much to his wife's dismay.

articles.title: The Dungeon Crawler Carl Graphic Novels Are Buy 2, Get 1 Free at Target
articles.body:
The Dungeon Crawler Carl books have been blowing up, in part because the LitRPG series is excellent in pretty much every format. The books are great, the audiobooks are wonderful, and now there's even a really cool graphic novel adaptation.

If you're looking to collect the first two volumes that have been released so far, Target has generously included them in its buy 2, get 1 free sale . The sale runs from now until Saturday October 10, and it also includes all of the Dungeon Crawler Carl books . It's a great time to add some DCC to your collection.

Dungeon Crawler Carl, Vol. 1 (Graphic Novel)

Dungeon Crawler Carl, Vol. 2 (Graphic Novel)

Target's sale includes both Volume 1 and Volume 2 of the graphic novel, while Amazon's competing sale only has the first one. That makes Target the overall better place to buy Dungeon Crawler Carl right now. You do need to add one more eligible book to take advantage of the full discount, but there's a lot to choose from within the sale.

Is The Dungeon Crawler Carl Graphic Novel Worth Reading?

As someone who has experienced Dungeon Crawler Carl in pretty much all of its forms, I can honestly say that the graphic novel is worth a read. I reviewed the first volume last month , and had nothing but positive things to say about it. Here's a quick summary of why I gave it an 8 out of 10:

"The first Dungeon Crawler Carl Graphic Novel turns Matt Dinniman's popular LitRPG into a chaotic flurry of action and achievements that just works. It's a great introduction to the story for those who don't want to read the books and feels additive for those who already have."

The Dungeon Crawler Carl graphic novels are actually just collected physical editions of the popular Webtoon series, so new pages are getting added pretty frequently. If you're only interested in the graphic novel editions of the comic, the good news is there's still more coming: Volume 3 of the adaptation is currently set to release on March 9, 2027.

With the Dungeon Crawler Carl TV series in the works and the popularity of the books continuing to grow, it seems likely that the graphic novel will continue until the story comes to an end.

Jacob Kienlen is a Senior Audience Development Strategist and Writer for IGN. Born and raised in Portland, Oregon, he has considered the Northwest his home for his entire life. With a bachelor's degree in communication and 10 years of professional writing experience, his expertise is spread across a variety of different pop culture topics — from TV series to books and the latest LEGO sets .

articles.title: This Fanatical Deal Drops Marathon on PC to $19.39, Cheaper Than Steam's Autumn Sale
articles.body:
Steam launched its Autumn Sale last week , and the PC-inclined know these seasonal sales are pretty much the best time of year to buy games. Sometimes, though, the gaming giant isn't offering the best possible price.

On Steam, Bungie’s latest live action release, Marathon, has dropped to $23.99 . However, digital game stores like Fanatical and GMG are also running fall sales, and it just so happens that the former has Marathon Steam codes for even cheaper, at $19.99 .

According to price trackers , that’s a lower price than the game has ever been on the U.S. side of Steam. Regardless of your feelings about the hardcore extraction shooter, it’s hard to argue with that being a good deal.

Marathon on PC Drops Under $20 at Fanatical

Fanatical is a UK-based e-commerce platform under the Fandom umbrella. It’s one of our go-to storefronts for digital game deals, so you can rest assured you’re paying for something legit. And yes, it’s a Steam code, not some wacky third-party launcher situation.

As for Marathon itself, well, the game’s been through a lot. The first couple of trailers picked up some buzz on social media, but a troubled alpha test and plagiarism allegations led to some delays . A little thing called Arc Raiders launched during that delay, creating even more competition in the multiplayer shooter space. Still, Marathon reworked some assets, and Bungie launched the game this past March.

While Marathon has faced challenges building a massive player base, the fans it does have are particularly dedicated. That dedication is likely owing to the shooter’s emphasis on hardcore gameplay and community, though the developers have recently outlined their plans to make the game more accessible with future updates, like a PVE mode .

I’ve put my fair share of time into the game and can attest to the difficulty allegations. There’s something addicting about that learning curve, though, especially with the loot and progression systems. At the end of the day, you get fresh Bungie gunplay in a disgustingly stylish world.

I think IGN’s Travis Northup said it best in his 9/10 review : “Marathon is unapproachable, unforgiving, offputtingly creepy, and has a playerbase of violent goblins who exist solely to bash your face in with a brick, and for all of these reasons it's become my favorite extraction shooter of all time.”

articles.title: Castlevania: Belmont's Curse Demo Hides Fighting Game Easter Eggs Behind Secret Weapon
articles.summary: The developers of Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse are wearing their love of fighting games on their sleeves, as eagle-eyed fans have spotted some unmistakable references to classic fighting game characters in its demo.
articles.body:
The developers of Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse are wearing their love of fighting games on their sleeves, as eagle-eyed fans have spotted some unmistakable references to classic fighting game characters in its demo.

Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse released a free demo on October 1, 2026, giving players a brief taste of what the game’s combat will look like. In this game, we take control of Rose Belmont, who navigates the ruined streets of 1500s Paris with a sword and her mother’s magical tarot cards.

If the demo is anything to go by, this game will be a treat for hardcore Metroidvania fans, as it includes a wealth of secret areas to uncover. One of these areas can be accessed in the demo, which gives you a pair of brass knuckle-style MMA gloves called Cestus. The weapon stacks on damage to enemies the more you hit them, encouraging players to go on the offensive.

After Rose finishes an attack using Cestus, she will strike a pose for a few seconds. These poses cycle seemingly at random, but they’re clearly intentional, and each boasts a unique animation. It didn’t take long for players to notice some striking similarities between these poses and the fighting stances of classic fighting game characters, of which there are a good handful.

Twitter/X user and Castlevania fan StockeTepes compiled these poses in a video, showing Rose settling into the idle poses for Ryu, Chun-Li, Oro, and Sagat, as well as Mai Shiranui and Akuma / Oni. Even Spider-Man’s iconic pose from Marvel vs Capcom 2 was included. Other fans pointed out that Rose’s air-to-air combo using Cestus mimics that of Akuma’s in-air fireball attack, Zanku Hadouken (or, in my opinion, M. Bison's Hell Attack).

Castlevania is a franchise known for tipping its hat to fighting games; if you’ve played Symphony of the Night, you’ll know that the inputs for Alucard’s purchasable spells read exactly like the motions for special moves in a fighting game, and the gauntlet-style weapon Fist of Tulkas basically let you throw out a Hadouken. And in Portrait of Ruin, players can unlock Martial Arts moves that give you special abilities, which require special fighting game-style inputs to pull off. Konami even released a Castlevania fighting game in 2008 called Castlevania Judgment (though whether or not it's remembered fondly is a matter of personal opinion).

I told you, Castlevania LOVES fighting games 🔥 And the tradition of calling back to them continues with Belmont's Curse! So I made a lil edit showcasing how the Demo's secret weapon, Cestus, homages idle poses for many of it's iconic characters. MUCH more coming stay tuned 😈 — 🖤 Stocke ❤️ (@StockeTepes) October 6, 2026

I told you, Castlevania LOVES fighting games 🔥 And the tradition of calling back to them continues with Belmont's Curse! So I made a lil edit showcasing how the Demo's secret weapon, Cestus, homages idle poses for many of it's iconic characters. MUCH more coming stay tuned 😈

Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse officially releases on October 15. In the meantime, there’s no shortage of Castlevania games for you to play as you wait for the latest entry in the series to launch. (My personal favorites are Symphony of the Night , Super Castlevania IV , and the OG Castlevania game — but there’s literally more than 30 to choose from!)

That’s not all; the iconic soundtrack of the Castlevania franchise is getting its own live power rock-symphony in March 2026, with showings in London, Tokyo, and Los Angeles. It’s a great time to be a Castlevania fan — but a terrible night to have a curse.

articles.title: Top 5 Robot Vacuum Deals for Prime Big Deal Days
articles.summary: Keep fall leaves, mud, and dirt off your floors with these hands-off cleaning picks.
articles.body:
It’s fall, and that means you and your family will likely be traipsing leaves and dirt all over the house. A robot vacuum can make cleanup ridiculously easy. All you’ll likely need to do is press a button on the device or use your phone to send the vacuum out to pick up the mess for you. With Amazon’s Prime Big Deal Days Sale happening until the end of the day today, many top robot vacuums are deeply discounted, so you can snag one cheaply and enjoy hands-off cleaning.

dreame D20 Air Plus Robot Vacuum and Mop

ECOVACS DEEBOT X12 OMNICYCLONE Robot Vacuum and Mop

Bissell FlexClean FurForce Robot Vac & Mop

roborock 2026 New Qrevo S Pro Robot Vacuum and Mop

I’ve tested my fair share of robot vacuums, and the deals I’ve selected above are from brands I know and love. Many of these devices also do more than vacuum, offering mopping functionality and even a base station for better self-sufficiency. The only catch is that you need to be an Amazon Prime member to score these awesome discounts. If you’re not, you can sign up here .

Dreame D20 Air Plus Back at Lowest Price

For something super capable and budget-friendly, get the Dreame D20 Air Plus. It’s only $199.99, back at its lowest price ever. Surprisingly, it delivers better suction power than some $1,000+ robot vacuums I’ve tested. It also mops with adjustable flow levels to keep your hard floors shining. Admittedly, the base station isn’t that high-tech, but it still self-empties the dust box for 120 days of hands-free debris collection.

Get $700 Off the Ecovacs Deebot X12 Omnicyclone

Ecovacs is one of my favorite robot vacuum brands, and it consistently delivers. While I haven’t tested the X12 yet, its features are impressive. A unique FocusJet breaks down larger messes before self-cleaning roller mops pick them up. For vacuuming, the 22,000Pa BLAST Suction and TruEdge 3.0 tech can suction clean debris in even hard-to-reach places. And the X12’s self-maintaining, fully automated OmniCyclone station makes for an almost completely hands-off clean.

Bissell has been in the vacuum game for a long time, and one of the brand's top robot vacuums got a steep discount for October Prime Day. The FlexClean FurForce Robot Vac & Mop is ideal for households with pets or kids. Anti-tangle brush rolls help prevent hair wrap, and it offers much stronger suction power than Bissell’s lower-end model. Mopping functionality is built-in, and the multi-surface formula that’s included will help better break down caked-on messes on hard floors.

If you don’t need all the bells and whistles and just want a simple robot vacuum for smaller spaces, grab the eufy 11S MAX. It’s down to just $133. It features a slim profile to reach under low furniture, plenty of suction power, and does a solid job evading obstacles. Given the budget, price, it doesn’t come with a base station or app control. articles.title: Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen Is a Great Expansion Full of Interesting Characters, Vibrant Enemies, and a Deep New Area to Explore - Review
articles.summary: An engrossing expansion full of interesting new characters and vibrant enemies.
articles.body:
The first Dark Arisen expansion for the original Dragon’s Dogma has a well-lauded place in video game history as the expansion that “fixed” the base game, sanding down the rough technical edges and tweaking things to make the notoriously obtuse RPG more approachable. It also added hours of new content, spiraling an already heady story directly into the heavens on the back of dragon wings. Dark Arisen 2 isn’t as transformational as the first one was, primarily because many of Dragon’s Dogma 2’s biggest issues have been fixed through incremental patching since it came out in 2024. But the new content here definitely flies in the same ambitious skies as its predecessor, pushing the story and world design to new heights, even if some of the new progression options get left behind.

As with Dragon’s Dogma 2’s base campaign, Dark Arisen 2’s story remixes themes from the first game without being a simple retelling. Like in the first, another Arisen has been rumored to exist, something that shouldn’t be possible and demands your immediate attention. This takes you north to the frozen mountains of Norgan, a place that is largely abandoned save for the single settlement at its border (and the steady stream of visitors coming from other lands to investigate what’s been lost under all that ice besides you).

The expansion’s story also meanders in similar ways to the base game, with plot points getting sidetracked by little tasks or other happenings, but it didn’t feel as distracting since a lot of the “help me and I’ll help you” quests are relegated to side stories. As a whole, this roughly 20-hour main quest is solid, lacking in nuanced writing or ground breaking storytelling but bursting with a tangibly broody mood, big moments, and some genuinely interesting lore. It’s meditation on how a hero of destiny chooses their fate (if they get a choice at all) is unsubtle, and spends far too long at the end really sending the message home, but it sticks it.

For those who don’t mind a lot of filler with their killer, there are plenty of people with tasks thoroughly less vital to the survival of reality that need doing. A couple of those quest lines stand out – one where you help the son of the village’s leader become brave and tough enough to follow in his footsteps, for example – but most are just a flimsy excuse to run around the world and beat up enemies.

The frigid Norgan region is delightfully dense with things to find and see even if its smaller than most other regions in Dragon’s Dogma 2. What it lacks in square footage on a map, it gains in a sprawling sense of height that stretches from it’s jagged icy peaks down to winding underground caverns that spread wide and interconnect. Navigating up and down the rocks is a treacherous and daunting road at first, but climbing hooks can be used on specific poles scattered throughout to bridge elevations without the fuss.

Combined with how dungeons and caves tended to loop back on themselves, revealing exits or opening doors that served as their own shortcuts into and out of zones, and Dark Arisen 2 felt almost like a Zelda or Metroid game in ways this series never has before. The abundance of portcrystals scattered around the map is another navigational relief. There are more in Norgan than there are in Vermund and Bathall combined, making travelling to different zones far more reasonable than it was in the base game.

Note that reasonable doesn’t necessarily mean easier. The portcrystal’s abundance is a practical matter, as ox carts wouldn’t last long in the harsh environments. Norgan’s wintry winds often pick up, turning snowfall into blinding whiteouts that threaten to freeze you to death if you aren’t protected by special winterized gear or new consumables designed to stave off these frost effects for a limited time. These came in abundance pretty regularly so I never felt like my life was in danger out there, but the scrambling effect it has on the minimap and how generally hard it is to see or navigate in real time made them a threat worth waiting out at camp.

Norgan’s crumbling castles and snowcapped cliffs are a welcome change of pace from the rolling hills and dense hinterlands of Vermund and he craggy deserts of Bathall. It’s also not all snowy wastes. I was surprised to see a break in the snow drifts when I came across a festering poisonous swamp. It matches thematically in that everything in it is dead (or maybe wishes it was), but areas like that and the crystal caves deep below the mountains subverted my expectations for the region in a welcome way.

The bulk of what you’ll find hidden in the snow are Spoils, a new gear type that appears in generic shapes (long weapon, aegis, etc.) at first, but is revealed to be a usable piece of equipment when appraised by one of the new NPCs. Rolling the dice for new gear was not particularly exciting, and it further isolated me from having any real attachment to my equipment in a game that already had an abundance of junk to constantly ignore. There are at least things outside of raw stats to consider, as each piece of gear can potentially have special attributes that grant passive abilities or enhance specific weapon skills – but no single piece of gear stayed in rotation long enough to be something I relied on much, with the deluge of experience points I received strapping a rocket to my leveling almost immediately. I can see how these could fit into an endgame grind, but participating in a lottery in hopes to get incrementally stronger as my levels reaches the mid 100s is the sort of loop that I, like The Arisen, simply don’t have the heart for.

New skills and abilities for every vocation can be learned from obelisks that dot the ridges and tundra in Norgan. Each have multiple tiers of offerings, and while the first are available for purchase with rift points immediately, the rest need to be unlocked with offering flames, earned in Dark Arisen 2’s second big campaign: the repeatable 12 Lost Rites dungeons scattered across Vermund and Bathall. Each skill is welcome, though outside some of the powerful new spells available to casters, I don’t think many of them change the balance of vocations in any significant way. Trickster is more active now that you can do additional things with your incense clone, like possess enemies and have them attack their kin. But if you have a favorite class, I’m not sure these new offerings will change the tier list already in your mind.

The Last Rites dungeons range from short gauntlets of monster battles to sizable delves deep into danger. Some have unique designs that lean on a particular mechanic or require specific prerequisites before you can enter them – one where your Arisen must be an Archer/Magick Archer and whose rooms are filled with shootable support pillars to help collapse terrain onto enemies stands out. I haven't finished them all, as some only appear during the last act of the original story, but I haven’t found any of the ones I have completed to be a significant challenge, especially with the enormous power spike granted from grinding through Norgan first. The new recurring boss from them, a giant Beholder-like eyeball monster, is a fun fight, though.

Norgan’s new slate of monsters can be pretty gnarly early on. Some are just stronger versions of baddies you’ve seen in the past, like the barbarous beocarns who are essentially just bigger bandits. But the brand new foes, like that baphomet-shaped lesser demons who sling spells and enhance their own physical attacks with elemental boons, can be pretty intense dance partners. Giant yetis with gaping mouths that stretch the length of their bodies might be some of the most grotesque and memorable enemies in the series. I really loved the little freaks hiding out in the tundra.

articles.title: Samuel L. Jackson Confirms Nick Fury Will Return in Avengers: Secret Wars
articles.summary: Samuel L. Jackson has confirmed that we won’t be seeing Nick Fury in Avengers: Doomsday, but said that his character is set to return in Avengers: Secret Wars.
articles.body:
Samuel L. Jackson has confirmed that we won’t be seeing Nick Fury in Avengers: Doomsday, but said that his character is set to return in Avengers: Secret Wars.

Jackson revealed this information in a red carpet interview with The Direct ahead of the premier for The Beast, his newest film. After The Direct’s interviewer noted that Nick Fury hasn’t been spotted in a Marvel movie for some time, Jackson said that he will be in the next film after Doomsday — which, according to the current slate laid out by Marvel Studios, is Avengers: Secret Wars.

He didn’t elaborate on what we can expect from Fury’s appearance in this movie, saying that Marvel only told him that he’d be in it and nothing more.

Secret Wars Gallery: God Emperor Doom Rules the Marvel Universe

"Next movie... [The] movie after this one,” he told the outlet. “I have no idea. [Marvel] hasn't told me anything, other than, 'You're not gonna be in this movie. You'll be in the next.'"

Thus far, Marvel has been keeping the cast of Secret Wars close to its chest; in September, Noah Jupe was added to the roster of actors set to star in the film in an as-yet unrevealed role. Anthony Mackie has also been confirmed for the movie, but says he won’t be able start filming until his run in a broadway showing of Macbeth ends in July 2027.

Secret Wars recently ran into some significant roadblocks, with multiple insiders claiming that filming for the project has been delayed until early 2027 , most likely in January. Thus far, no reason for this delay has been revealed, but it’s enough to spark anxiety among fans — many of whom feel that Doomsday needs to be a home run of a movie to keep interest in the current MCU saga.

Secret Wars is set to cap off the Russo brothers’ involvement with the MCU, with the two saying in June 2026 that they won’t be directing a third film to create a new Avengers trilogy. The movie marks the sixth major cross-over event in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, and will serve as the final chapter in the Multiverse saga, putting an end to the innumerable variations of characters that have been popping up in Marvel’s TV series and films over the MCU’s last three phases.

Recent reporting indicates that the Battleworld will be involved somehow, given that it serves as the setting for the Secret Wars comic storyline, though this hasn’t been confirmed. It would be a fitting way for the Multiverse Saga to end, though, as Battleworld is a patchwork planet made up of several different versions of Earth combined by none other than Dr Doom.

For now, we’ll just have to wait and see what’s in store, and if Avengers: Doomsday lives up to the hype. The movie releases in theaters on December 18, 2026.

articles.title: Para-shooters allege corruption in Asian Games selection; PCI chief says process ‘100% fair’
articles.summary: The selection of India’s para-shooting team for the Aichi-Nagoya Para Asian Games has come under a cloud of controversy after a group of para-shooters
articles.body: The selection of India’s para-shooting team for the Aichi-Nagoya Para Asian Games has come under a cloud of controversy after a group of para-shooters alleged corruption and financial demands in the selection process.The shooters have sought an independent inquiry into what they described as financial corruption, extortion and manipulation by officials of the Paralympic Committee of India (PCI) and its Shooting Technical Committee (STC).In a representation submitted to the Director General of the Sports Authority of India (SAI) on Wednesday, the athletes alleged “illicit monetary extortion”, “brazen corruption” and violations of Sports Ministry guidelines.The Para Asian Games are scheduled to be held from October 18 to 24.Shooters allege 20 per cent demandOne of the most serious allegations made in the representation was that athletes were being asked to give 20 per cent of their government cash awards as a condition for being selected for the national team.“Athletes are being coerced under severe duress into paying an illegal kickback of 20 per cent of their sanctioned government cash awards to designated committee office-bearers as a mandatory pre-condition for national team selection,” the representation alleged.The shooters also alleged that international quota places were not allocated purely on rankings and performances. They claimed financial considerations played a role in deciding who received the available places.According to their representation, two of the 15 international quota places available to India were surrendered because athletes next in line allegedly refused to meet the financial demands. The athletes also accused the selection committee of changing qualifying scores, ignoring Sports Ministry criteria and replacing an earlier selection panel without giving a recorded reason.Sandeep Kumar alleges selection biasP4 50m free pistol SH1 shooter Sandeep Kumar, ranked third in Asia, also questioned the selection decisions. He alleged that Rudrankksh Khandelwal, ranked 14th in Asia, was picked ahead of Akash, the Asian No. 1, and himself. Sandeep said he was “deeply aggrieved” by what he described as arbitrary decisions and violations of the selection rules.The shooters also questioned the appointment of an individual as a technical expert and Director of Operations, alleging that the person had no record of competing in an official shooting event.PCI rejects all allegationsPCI president Devendra Jhajharia strongly rejected the charges and said the team had been selected strictly according to the prescribed rules.“The selection has been done as per the criteria. There has been no discrimination against anyone. The selections are 100 per cent fair and according to the Sports Ministry’s guidelines,” Jhajharia, a two-time Paralympics javelin gold-medallist, told PTI.Jhajharia also rejected Sandeep’s allegation that he was left out to make way for a shooter who had links with the coach.“Those are all false allegations,” Jhajharia said.Ministry says grievances will be examinedA Sports Ministry source said genuine complaints raised by the para-shooters would be looked into. However, the source added that the Indian team for the Para Asian Games had already been finalised and could not be changed at this stage.The shooters have also indicated that they could take the matter to court if their allegations are not addressed.They said they may approach the High Court under Article 226 of the Constitution, seeking a writ of mandamus and a court-monitored investigation into the selection process.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mixtape Wins Game of the Year at the 2026 Australian Game Developer Awards
articles.summary: Mixtape developer Beethoven & Dinosaur has won a trifecta of awards at the 2026 AGDAs, including Excellence in Visual Art, Excellence in Sound Design, and Game of the Year.
articles.body:
Melbourne-based studio Beethoven & Dinosaur has won Game of the Year for its music-themed, minigame-driven adventure game Mixtape at the 2026 Australian Game Developer Awards (AGDAs). Mixtape also won Excellence in Visual Art and Excellence in Sound Design.

“Mixtape was the outcome of an amazingly talented team,” said Beethoven & Dinosaur director Johnny Galvatron. “To go from wanting to make a game around Devo to creating something that resonates with so many people is mind blowing. We’re lucky to be part of such a talented community, and I’m so proud of Mixtape and my team.”

Other winners from this year’s AGDAs include rhythm game Bits & Bops from Tempo Lab Games for both Excellence in Gameplay and Excellence in Accessibility, and puzzle platformer Schrodinger’s Cat Burglar from Abandoned Sheep for Excellence in Narrative. The Studio of the Year was awarded to Canberra-based Uppercut Games.

articles.title: Dodgers’ Next Playoff Opponent Revealed
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers defeated the Atlanta Braves in the NLDS, and now they've learned who they'll face next.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers downed the Atlanta Braves 4-1 on Wednesday , locking up a spot in the National League Championship Series in the process.

So who will the Dodgers face next? The other NLDS is over as well, so we have an answer.

With their win on Wednesday night, the Milwaukee Brewers are moving on to face the Dodgers.

The Brewers closed out a 3-1 series win at Petco Park in San Diego, and as the top seed in the National League, they'll host the first two games of the NLCS.

The Dodgers and Brewers split the regular season with four victories apiece, but when it matters most, the Dodgers have had the edge.

In last year's NLCS, the Dodgers swept the Brewers in four games, including a huge performance from Shohei Ohtani in Game 4 .

Not only did he throw six scoreless innings with 10 strikeouts, but he hit three monster home runs.

This Brewers team, though, is led by Jacob Misiorowski, the hard-throwing righty who routinely tops 104 mph.

He's also the presumptive winner of the NL Cy Young Award, an honor coveted by Dodgers superstar Ohtani.

Ohtani hasn't been playing great these playoffs, but perhaps that will fuel his fire and bring out his best against the Brewers

Game 1 of the NLCS is set for Sunday, Oct. 11.

The time for first pitch hasn't yet been announced.

The Dodgers' starting pitcher also hasn't been announced yet, but given that newly acquired superstar Tarik Skubal started Game 1 of the NLDS, it seems likely that he could take the mound first again.

That said, Yoshinobu Yamamoto started Game 3 for the Dodgers on Tuesday, giving him five days' rest for Sunday if manager Dave Roberts wants to go that route instead.

Who do you want to see start Game 1 for the Dodgers? Are you excited to be facing off with the Brewers again with a pennant on the line?

articles.title: Tatis, Padres eliminated from postseason by top-seeded Brewers in 4 games
articles.summary: SAN DIEGO (AP) — Fernando Tatis Jr.'s 429-foot home run to straightaway center field leading off the third inning got the sellout crowd of 47,712 at Petco Pa...
articles.body:
SAN DIEGO (AP) — Fernando Tatis Jr.'s 429-foot home run to straightaway center field leading off the third inning got the sellout crowd of 47,712 at Petco Park revved up and waving their yellow rally towels.

That was pretty much the extent of the excitement for those fans as the Padres once again fell short of winning their first World Series.

Tatis' second homer of the postseason tied the game at 1, but the Milwaukee Brewers went on to win 3-1 Wednesday night to take their best-of-five NL Division Series in four games.

Manny Machado nearly tied it with a two-run homer in the eighth, but Garrett Mitchell made the catch at the center-field fence to rob him.

With the crowd on its feet still hoping for a comeback, pinch-hitter Gavin Sheets struck out to end it and the Brewers had a muted celebration on the field.

While the top-seeded Brewers head home to get ready to host the Padres' biggest rivals, the Los Angeles Dodgers, in Game 1 of the National League Championship Series, the Padres head off into an uncertain offseason.

New owners José E. Feliciano and Kwanza Jones brought an exciting vibe to the team when they took over in late August. Now it's up to them to back general manager A.J. Preller in trying to get San Diego that elusive World Series title.

The Padres haven't been to the Fall Classic since making it for a second time in 1998. They didn't win either one.

This year, their third consecutive 90-win season carried them into the playoffs for the third straight autumn, both club records.

They did it behind rookie manager Craig Stammen, a surprise hire last fall after Mike Shildt retired less than two weeks after the Padres were eliminated by the Chicago Cubs 2-1 in the wild-card round.

The Padres struggled so much during the first half that fans wondered if Preller would trade fireballing closer Mason Miller. But he kept Miller and the Padres turned it on in the second half to reach the postseason.

They beat the Cubs in two games at Petco Park last week to sweep their Wild Card Series before losing two close, riveting games in Milwaukee.

San Diego stayed alive with a 4-3 win Tuesday night in which Michael King, the Game 2 starter, earned a two-inning save on one day of rest to extend the season one more night.

Prime Video has confirmed a new, one-off episode of its Clarkson’s Farm series, which will see host Jeremy Clarkson temporarily return to his Top Gear and The Grand Tour roots for an automotive-themed special.

Jeremy Grows a Car: A Clarkson’s Farm Special will see Clarkson attempt what Prime proposes is a world first: he will grow and build his own car from produce sourced from his personal farm, Diddly Squat.

Using the Jaguar F-Type V6S as his base, Clarkson will be restoring it using his own Diddly leather interior and wool carpets, and will also be attempting to grow a crop of flax fiber to turn into a sustainable flax-composite material – an alternative to carbon fiber Prime claims is already on the radar of major car makers.

articles.title: Brewers survive Game 4 thriller to advance to NLCS
articles.summary: Jackson Chourio delivered another clutch RBI and the pitching staff was strong again as the Brewers eliminated the Padres in their NL Division Series.
articles.body:
SAN DIEGO – The Milwaukee Brewers are onto the National League Championship Series for the second straight year.

The Brewers snapped a 12-game road losing streak in the postseason that tied the all-time record in Major League Baseball in their own fashion Oct. 8 at Petco Park, littering the bases with runners all night and overpowering the San Diego Padres with their arms for a 3-1 victory in Game 4 of the National League Division Series.

Here are three immediate takeaways from the clincher.

Jackson Chourio sets franchise record with another clutch hit

At age 22, Jackson Chourio has quite the case for greatest postseason performer in franchise history.With his rocket back up the middle to score Garrett Mitchell in the fifth, Chourio drove in his 17th career playoff run, most ever by a Brewers player.

Mitchell led off the inning by dragging a triple over the first base bag, missing a foul ball by inches, and scooting to third. That was the final pitch thrown by reliever Robbie Ray, who was replaced by Bradgley Rodriguez, the flamethrower who has been Milwaukee's nemesis in the middle innings this series.

After a Joey Ortiz chopper right to third, Chourio got the run home by peppering a fastball in off the plate just past Jake Cronenworth's glove up the middle.

That gave Chourio 17 postseason RBI, surpassing Ryan Braun's mark of 16. Chourio did it in 16 games, whereas Braun played in 27.

Chourio set the franchise record for postseason home runs with his fifth all-time in Game 1 of the series against Ray.

Many pitchers have owed Joey Ortiz a nice dinner for his fine defensive work on the infield. But this time, Ortiz is the one who owes it.

With one out and runners on first and second in the bottom of the first, Ortiz opted not to throw to first to complete what appeared to be an almost-surefire double play after taking a Ty France grounder to third base for a force.

It wasn't initially clear what Ortiz was thinking. It didn't seem that he forgot how many outs there were, as his first move was back toward the mound rather than the dugout.

Starting pitcher Robert Gasser then walked Austin Hays to load the bases but escaped what could have been a disastrous situation by getting Xander Bogaerts to pop out for the third out.

The game could have easily swung in San Diego's favor and gotten the third-largest crowd in stadium history into it early; instead, Gasser settled in and lasted four innings, allowing a Fernando Tatis Jr. solo homer to lead off the third and nothing more.

Aaron Ashby may have been the game's MVP

Aaron Ashby led all National League relievers in innings pitched with 87 in the regular season but never got more than eight outs in a single game – until now.

Pat Murphy's personal RAV4 entered with nobody out in the fifth and didn't depart until he completed the bottom of the seventh by freezing pinch-hitter Miguel Andujar on a curveball.

Ashby's nine outs bridged the game from Gasser to Abner Uribe, and featured some of his best pitching when the moment called for it.

He struck out Samad Taylor swinging on a down-and-away changeup that had been set up perfectly by a sinker and curve. The next three hitters at the top of the Padres order grounded out before Ty France worked a one-out walk in the sixth.

Next came Ashby's best sequence of the night. Austin Hays, in the lineup to be a lefty masher, sold out for a sinker and waved at a first-pitch changeup. William Contreras called for another, which Ashby spiked, but that didn't deter him from going back to it again. Ashby got another whiff on a changeup to go ahead, 1-2. To put Hays away, Contreras called for a curveball – staying off-speed but a movement profile to get Hays to swing over it.

It worked according to plan. Hays chopped a one-hopper right to Ashby, who started an inning-ending 1-4-3 double play.

The Padres put the tying run at the plate with two outs in the seventh when Jake Cronenworth walked on a full count, but the curveball worked exquisitely for Ashby again as he caught Taylor looking for velocity and spun two in a row in the zone that left the San Diego left fielder browsing.

It has been a postseason of October redemption for Ashby

articles.title: The Aces are on the ropes; need a historic turnaround to keep title defense alive
articles.summary: SAN FRANCISCO – If the Las Vegas Aces are going to repeat again, they will have to do something that has never been done before.
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO – If the Las Vegas Aces are going to repeat again, they will have to do something that has never been done before.

Three-time champions in the last four years — boasting a soon-to-be five-time MVP in their ranks — the No. 3 Aces aren't foreign to historic feats.

However, overcoming a 2-0 deficit in a WNBA postseason is literally unprecedented. And that's the hole the reigning queens find themselves in after losing Game 2 of the semifinals to the No. 2 Golden State Valkyries, 83-81, Wednesday night.

Initially, a nightmare repeat of the Game 1, 71-60, defeat from Sunday looked to be on the cards. The Aces trailed by as many as 17 before outscoring the Valkyries 26-17 in the fourth quarter, making things extremely interesting.

Perhaps more interesting than the electric Ballhalla would have liked it. But it made for an epic crescendo for the locals.

For the Aces, things looked better in the second half, but not enough to knock off a young team starving for success — and wanting your crown — despite being in existence for less than two years.

Head coach Becky Hammon called the first half "abysmal." She wants more of what she saw after the interval.

"They still out-rebounded us, but [we were] better," she said. The Aces suffered the largest rebounding deficit (-27) in franchise history in the first game. The Valkyries had only four more boards tonight (29-25), but it was still an edge.

The Aces got a positive impact off the bench from Kalani Brown in 23 minutes, grabbing eight boards and adding nine points. But the entire team still needs to do much more.

"We all have to box out," Brown said. "It's not just their post players getting [rebounds]; it's their guards flying in there, too. They're a very scrappy team, and we just have to be scrappy with them… Those 50/50 balls, we just have to have those."

At this stage, beyond the glass wars, the biggest difference maker in the series has been effort. Neither team is shooting lights out or playing flawless basketball. But the Valkyries have just been a half step ahead. Their defense — best in the league as advertised — is disruptive from start to finish, almost like head coach Natalie Nakase recharges her players' batteries at every timeout.

The Aces are older and much richer in experience, but they're fighting injuries left and right. Still, they're too seasoned in these scenarios not to come through. The way Golden State has derailed the Aces' entire offensive flow, two games in a row, jumps off the page.

The Valkyries still have a lot of work to do to sweep the Aces. But the Aces so rarely even lose two games in a row. This almost feels different. A passing of the torch? No. A'ja Wilson and Jackie Young are in the middle of their primes.

However, Golden State's rising star Gabby Williams has something A'ja Wilson and Jackie Young don't: reliable help.

Williams isn't expected to drop 30 a game for the Valkyries to win. Nakase takes pride in her team's strength in numbers. A different player can carry them any given night. The Aces currently can't win if A'ja doesn't reach that mark.

Williams ended with 20 points, one of three Valkyries in double figures. Kayla Thornton (3-5 3PT) added 16, and former Ace Tiffany Hayes erupted for 21 points (6-for-10 FG) in 16 minutes off the bench. Golden State's bench bettered Vegas' 34-14.

Wilson improved on her 24 points on 21 shots from Game 1, pouring in 24 on 9-for-16 shooting today. Young (14) and Gray (19) elevated their 27 combined points from the opener, but Young's 6-for-22 shooting across the two games isn't going to cut it. The Aces need more from their Swiss Army knife.

Young showed flashes of what everyone knows she brings late. She knocked in a three-pointer, and another from the returning Stephanie Talbot followed, making it a seven-point game with 8:20 remaining in the fourth.

And even though the Aces couldn't string together consecutive stops when they needed them, they kept chipping into the Valkyries' weakening shield.

The visitors took a brief 76-74 lead with about two minutes remaining — courtesy of triples from Dana Evans, back after a five-game absence, and Gray, plus a nice finish inside from Wilson on former teammate Kiah Stokes.

The Valkyries didn't blink, though. Acting like they've been here before, Williams got to her spot with ease to bring it back level, and an audacious 28-foot deep three from Veronica Burton — her first bucket of the night (1-for-3 FG) — gave Golden State its lead back, 79-76, with 41.5 ticks left to play. And it was one the hosts would not relinquish again.

The frenzy Burton sent Ballhalla into had the building shaking. Literally. Neither the players nor the fans are afraid of the Aces' championship allure. They are ready for the moment.

Burton, the Valkyries' floor general, had a poor Game 1 and a similarly anonymous Game 2. She chipped in 12 points on 5-for-21 shooting across the two. However, with all the chips pushed into the middle of the table, she found her hot hand.

With the series now relocating to Sin City, a place where famously 'The House' always wins, the Aces will need their big hitters to ride their luck if they are to keep their season alive and return to San Francisco for a decisive Game 5 next Wednesday.

articles.title: Tom Cruise’s Digger Reportedly Positioned to Lose $250 Million
articles.body:
Divisive climate change satire Digger is set to lose $250 million by the end of its run, according to TheWrap. TheWrap claims insiders at new Warner Bros. overlords Skydance are not anticipating Digger will exceed a worldwide box office total of $40 million following its alarming opening weekend results (just $8 million in US domestic takings and a further $12 million in international receipts).

Warner Bros. has not commented on the claims. Warner Bros., which is being acquired by Paramount in a controversial $110 billion deal, will now exist alongside the latter under parent company Skydance.

Directed by back-to-back Best Director Oscar winner Alejandro G. Iñárritu (Birdman, The Revenant) and starring screen legend Tom Cruise, Digger has split both critics and audiences. Attempts have been made to weaponise the mixed reaction to its favour , but it doesn’t appear to have translated to increased interest in the film at the box office. IGN’s review notes Digger has “the budget to let some very talented artists work at the top of their game” but stresses it’s “far from a must-watch.”

articles.title: Below Review: Josh Hartnett Is Great, but the Netflix Small-Town Seaside Horror Series Can't Sustain Its Compelling Premise
articles.summary: Below is Netflix’s go at a “What if Jaws but…” type of story set in Newfoundland starring Josh Hartnett that starts off with a promising hook and closes with a hole-y, disappointing end.
articles.body:
Set in a tiny, remote coastal town that’s suddenly facing a mysterious threat from the sea, Netflix’s new drama/horror series Below is in the unfortunate position of being compared to Widow’s Bay, the other show that already did that this year. It’s a “what if Jaws but…” vehicle for Josh Hartnett, on a career upswing with things like Oppenheimer , Trap (yes, Trap), and a great episode of Black Mirror . And while he’s doing all he can here, in a thick Newfoundland accent no less, to carry the six-episode series, Below can’t keep pace with the other show. A relatively solid first half of episodes is done in by the back three that messily (and occasionally ridiculously) tie up a story that hasn’t fully found its sea legs.

Hartnett stars as Calvin Penney, a man with a trauma-filled life dating back to his family’s forced resettlement from one remote town to the slightly less remote town of Snook’s Arm (which, in real life, was resettled in 2018). As seen in the opening scene from 1986, a young Calvin, his sister Ruth, his mother, father, and a resettlement officer tow the Penny family’s whole-ass house behind a tiny, puttering boat. But something terrible happens; the Penny’s house is pulled under water and Calvin’s father, Leo, goes down with it, and Calvin cuts the line from the house to the boat to save the rest of his family. During this accident, Calvin sees something in the water — a cliché that isn’t just used as marketing for Below, but is repeated several times throughout the series — that looks like a void. Or rather, the gigantic eye of a very large beast that lives in these waters.

Fast forward 40 years and a Hartnett-aged Calvin is still living in Snook’s Arm, now a widow, hauling pieces of flaked-off iceberg back to the docks to sell to make into iceberg vodka (also a real thing). A family called the Crockers owns the distillery, owns Calvin’s boat, and has investments in seemingly every darned thing in sight, including the nearby Ocean Science Center where lead researcher Dr. Fonda Howander (Mackenzie Davis) studies marine samples and odd wildlife occurrences, like a flamingo landing on a resident’s roof. If you haven’t already guessed it, Below is about climate change and capitalism and what we’ve lost and what we can still preserve now that both of these things have become an insidious part of life. It’s just that Below doesn’t offer much more insight into these themes beyond broadly gesturing to the landscape and saying, with gumption, “ look .”

It’s a shame its thesis is so shallow because it really does begin with a promising hook: A massive chunk of iceberg floats into Snook’s Arm harbor, but the ice from it, which could be a cash cow for the local ice harvesters, oddly isn’t right. At the same time, animals and people start mysteriously dying when they’re near the water (don’t forget, something’s in it!), and the first episode ends on a shocking image I won’t spoil. What is distinctly interesting about Below is that it lets you think the provenance of all the suspicious goings-on could be anything, real or mystical, before revealing that, actually, they can all be explained with science — marine zoobiology, to be specific — or, of course, the avarice of capitalism.

Below takes place during a Come Home Year, wherein residents and family who have scattered return for festivities and local traditions like kissing fish in Snook’s Arm’s one and only dive bar. Calvin has his mushroom-addled son, Wade (Charlie Heaton), still living with him at home — Hartnett and Heaton’s scenes together are some of the strongest in Below — but his other two 20-something kids who left the roost, Mary (Ruby Stokes) and Jay (Rohan Campbell), come back too, each with their own cosmopolitan issues.

Mary has a boyfriend she desperately wants her dad to like and Jay seems to be in some shit, getting texted threats like, “Your [sic] a dead man.” (Typos, very scary.) As the season wears on, the Penny family bench catches a severe case of too much and not enough, where nearly everyone’s arc could have used a lot more attention with a couple more episodes.

Below takes an especially wild turn in Episode 4 — that includes a deep-water scene that I kind of can’t believe exists in the context of some other not-so-distant real-life events — and everything that follows plays out as rushed attempts to provide answers to the series’ questions. There are some answers, sure, but they aren’t particularly satisfying. And it’s still full of holes, enough to sink a boat.

articles.title: Wardogs Streamer Banned for Exploiting the Game's Building Mechanics to Get Rich
articles.summary: A vtuber is at the center of a controversy in the Wardogs community surrounding exploits.
articles.body:
A vtuber is at the center of a controversy in the Wardogs community surrounding exploits. The first-person shooter allows players to roleplay as a part of the war effort, taking to the front lines, running logistics in trucks, and building forward-operating bases (FOB) for their allies to control sections of the map.

Everything a player does — from recon to taxi driving their soldiers back into battle — earns them in-game money as a merc, which can then be spent on unlocking equipment and better loadouts. At the end of the season (or whenever the player chooses to trade their ill-gotten merc gains), money left over is converted into gold — a fluctuating economy of premium currency that can be spent on cosmetics.

Streamer KatieRouu was banned from the game for using exploits to take advantage of these systems. The streamer and their friends would place dozens of sniper lookout towers around a FOB and purposely let the enemy team take the base over, switching those buildings to enemy control.

even someone in the squad @KatieRouu was playing with knew what they were doing is not allowed and she dismisses his statement as if what she's doing is perfectly fine... then proceeded to go against the CEO for her ban on a post saying "So tell me what the exploit was." lol — waterrox (@WATERR0X) October 8, 2026

even someone in the squad @KatieRouu was playing with knew what they were doing is not allowed and she dismisses his statement as if what she's doing is perfectly fine... then proceeded to go against the CEO for her ban on a post saying "So tell me what the exploit was." lol

Once control was switched to the enemy team, KatieRouu and their squad would sit in another FOB that they’d supplied with ammunition, firing mortars at the base they'd allowed to be captured. With the money generated from destroying enemy structures and the money gained from assists (from supplying the ammo to the new base), the squad would rack up big money without actually contributing to their team’s war effort.

Joe Brammer, the CEO of Wardogs developer Bulkhead, responded to the ban : “Hey Katie, firstly thanks for streaming Wardogs. From what we can see you’ve been a completely regular player and someone who’s supported the game.

“Secondly, let’s be real here. You know it, I know it… you were taking advantage of an exploit. It’s obviously not an intended part of the game, had you raised it to us that’d be great… but running up millions for lots of players and promoting the exploit was absolutely not on. We can see that lots of the players involved immediately converted the cash they’d made via the exploit into gold bars and purchasing skins… so there was no gameplay there, nothing organic, purely a cash loop that you took advantage of.

“I wasn’t directly involved but I can see the ban team acted appropriately, if anything they were lenient compared to what we had said on Steam. This exploit has been fixed for Season 2 . We have also added data tracking for the behaviour and events now.

“Sorry for the ban, I can see you were going to stream tonight, but the rules are there for a reason. Hope we can at the very least, agree to disagree.

While some players have defended the streamer, arguing that they used legitimate game mechanics to generate the money, the Wardogs developer reiterated its stance. “We made it clear that known cash & xp exploit abuse will no longer be tolerated,” the official account posted on Twitter . “These punishments will stand. This decision is final.”

articles.title: CBS News Amazed by Accuracy of GTA 6, Highlights Miami Similarities in New Report
articles.summary: CBS News has reported on the accuracy of GTA 6’s Vice City, a fictionalized recreation of The Magic City. The Miami office of CBS News looked at major locations and brings on experts to talk about how accurate Rockstar’s open world is, from PortMiami to South Beach, Wynwood to the Everglades.
articles.body:
CBS News has reported on the accuracy of GTA 6’s Vice City, a fictionalized recreation of The Magic City. The Miami office of CBS News looked at major locations and brings on experts to talk about how accurate Rockstar’s open world is, from PortMiami to South Beach, Wynwood to the Everglades.

According to the report, fans have noticed over 100 locations in Vice City that mirror real areas in Miami, such as the Kaseya Center , home of NBA team the Miami Heat. The Heat will actually wear Vice City-themed uniforms in an upcoming match to celebrate the game’s launch in November.

“Vice City is unmistakably Miami,” the reporter says in the video before pausing the gameplay to compare it to the real street, 15th and Biscayne in downtown Miami. “If you’re a true Miami local, you’ll recognize that replicated overhead walkway.”

🚨 CBS MIAMI JUST HIGHLIGHTED GTA 6’S INCREDIBLE MIAMI ACCURACY. 🌴 GTA 6 fans have already spotted 100+ real Miami locations recreated in Vice City. From South Beach and PortMiami to Wynwood and the Everglades, Rockstar has recreated huge parts of Miami with an insane level of detail. Even specific streets and landmarks have been identified from the trailers. 👀🔥 Vice City might be the closest GTA has ever come to feeling like a real city. #GTA6 #GTAVI #RockstarGames Source: CBS Miami — Davin (@davngta) October 7, 2026

🚨 CBS MIAMI JUST HIGHLIGHTED GTA 6’S INCREDIBLE MIAMI ACCURACY. 🌴 GTA 6 fans have already spotted 100+ real Miami locations recreated in Vice City. From South Beach and PortMiami to Wynwood and the Everglades, Rockstar has recreated huge parts of Miami with an insane level of detail. Even specific streets and landmarks have been identified from the trailers. 👀🔥 Vice City might be the closest GTA has ever come to feeling like a real city. #GTA6 #GTAVI #RockstarGames Source: CBS Miami

The video moves onto Ocean Drive, an area of Miami players will recognize from the original GTA: Vice City, with its neon lights and bustling streets. The real life Breakwater Hotel appears in GTA 6 as Hotel Boardwalk, while a hotel in the background of the scene is called Hotel Dixon.

Hotel Dixon is a reimagined Victor Hotel. Miami Design Preservation League’s Julie Fornary appeared in the report to explain that the Victor Hotel was built by designer and architect L. Murray Dixon in 1937 — Rockstar’s naming choice here works as a layered Easter egg for Miami residents to pick up on, in a lovely homage to locals.

The report praises Rockstar’s attention to detail throughout, and how GTA 6 blends the iconic art deco architecture of Old Miami with the more modern buildings that dominate the city’s skyline. “But the game’s South Florida feel is deeper than just some buildings and streets,” the reporter says. “It’s what Vice City represents: character, culture, adventure. That same spirit has been part of Miami’s story from the very beginning.” Fornary goes on to talk about the city’s history and how it was founded by pioneers and adventurers.

GTA 6 gameplay and screenshots have already teased how the game will adapt Florida, known as Leonida in-game. The GTA 6 map has six different regions: Vice City, of course; Leonida Keys; Grassrivers; Port Gellhorn; Ambrosia; and Mount Kalaga National Park. Activities include kayaking, street and off-road racing, and air boating. We’ve also seen nightclub gameplay, beach gameplay, and plenty more.

Rockstar traveled across Florida with gang members and cops for GTA 6 research , embedding themselves in the scene. From the most affluent areas to the poor districts, the development team lived Miami to bottle up its essence in a sprawling open world crime drama. Yes, that also involved going to real-world strip clubs .

articles.title: Wizards of the Coast Confirms Reprints for Popular MTG Warhammer 40K Commander Decks
articles.summary: In a statement to IGN, Wizards of the Coast has confirmed a new "small" reprint run for the incredibly popular MTG Warhammer 40K Commander Decks.
articles.body:
Wizards of the Coast has told IGN that its Magic: The Gathering Warhammer 40K Commander Decks, originally printed in 2022 as part of the Universes Beyond series, have seen a fresh print run and will be available for order again soon.

The four decks, which marked the first precons beyond Magic’s own universe, were well-received at launch but have largely been relegated to the secondary market. The decks currently rack up high resale prices, costing hundreds of dollars at marketplace retailers like TCGplayer.

Magic’s Warhammer 40K Decks Are Coming Back

Following reports of game stores being able to order the Warhammer 40K precon decks via their order forms, IGN reached out to Wizards of the Coast for comment.

"Yes, we can confirm that we did a small reprint of the Commander decks that will be available to distributors and stores soon,” a Wizards of the Coast spokesperson said.

“Fans and WPN retailers should check with their distributors for availability, as it may vary by region."

The four decks each focus on a specific faction of the Warhammer 40K lore, established in Games Workshop’s miniature wargame universe. Ruinous Powers is a Chaos deck, Tyranid Swarm is all about the xenomorph-like Tyranids, Necron Dynasty is a mono-black deck that leans into the mysterious undead machines, while Forces of the Imperium is focused on, well, the Imperial forces.

Commander Deck Case (4 Decks - Collector's Edition)

Warhammer 40,000 - Forces of the Imperium

Before the decks launched, Magic's head designer, Mark Rosewater, said in a blog post, "There are no current plans to make in-universe Magic versions of the new cards in the Warhammer 40K Commander decks (we make in-universe ones for the Secret Lair cards), but we have the capability to do it if needed on a card-by-card basis."

That means that while it's possible that cards exclusive to the decks could be reprinted with in-universe artwork and names, a reprint should make all four much easier for collectors to get hold of. And while this is only a "small" reprint, adding more copies to the market could take some of the heat out of resale prices as well.

Although, Wizards’ statement did not confirm whether the all-foil Collector’s Edition versions of the decks would also be reprinted. There is also no word on how much any of the reprinted decks will cost (each originally retailed with a $59.99 MSRP). Nevertheless, if you’ve been waiting for any of the four, it looks as though your patience will be rewarded.

Warhammer 40K is in sharp focus at the moment. Dawn of War IV will bring the RTS franchise back this December, while Total War: Warhammer 40K is also slated for release next year. Henry Cavill's Warhammer 40K cinematic universe is also moving forward .

Lloyd Coombes is an experienced freelancer in tech, gaming and fitness seen at Polygon, Eurogamer, Macworld, TechRadar and many more. He's a big fan of Magic: The Gathering and other collectible card games, much to his wife's dismay.

articles.title: The Australian Government Helps Workers Know Their Rights for Taking Time Off for GTA 6
articles.summary: Australia's workplace regulator, The Fair Work Ombudsman, has put out a helpful graphic for people who might want to take time off when GTA 6 comes out this November.
articles.body:
Australia's workplace regulator, The Fair Work Ombudsman, has put out a helpful graphic for people who might want to take time off when GTA 6 comes out this November. “Let’s pretend GTA 6 is coming out tomorrow, but you don’t have any paid leave available to play on launch day” the graphic says. “Can you take unpaid leave?”

According to the Ombudsman, the National Employment Standards give Australians the right to unpaid leave “under specific circumstances.” So what are those circumstances? Being a carer is one, but that obviously doesn’t apply to playing an open world video game. Helping out with an emergency is another you can scratch off.

We got the Australian Government posting about different ways to take leave for GTA 6. No other game will ever match the hype. — GTA 6 Countdown ⏳ (@GTAVI_Countdown) October 8, 2026
