Having a child is another valid reason, but even if you worked at Rockstar you’d be hard pressed to argue for GTA 6 being your spawn. Luckily, you can just ask your boss, apparently. If your boss is nice, they’ll give you time off and you can come to an agreement. Is my boss nice? No, he will make me write news stories about it all day.

It’s quite a funny little graphic. The images feature a loved one in a hospital bed, with someone pressing the back of their hand to their head. Except it’s a copy of GTA 6 instead of a head. In the section about children, GTA 6 is on the ultrasound display.

It’s all very daft and tongue-in-cheek, but it speaks to the massive impact GTA 6 is going to have across the world. Rockstar traveled across Florida with gang members and cops for GTA 6 research , in an attempt to deliver the most authentic Miami mood possible. The team spared no expense, which is probably why GTA 6 reportedly cost around $1.5 billion to make , and that’s before factoring in marketing spend.

articles.title: Hellraiser: Revival Review
articles.summary: While the studded scalp of otherworld antagonist Pinhead absolutely looks the part, it’s a shame that little else in Hellraiser: Revival has been nailed to anywhere near the same extent.
articles.body:
From the opening scene of Hellraiser: Revival, in which an intimate moment of sexual fetishism goes horribly wrong for its hero and his lover, this survival horror adventure inspired by Clive Barker’s bloodsoaked ode to BDSM makes it painfully clear that it’s not for the squeamish. So graphic is its ebb and flow between blasting gory holes and bathroom glory holes that the greatest moments of tension I felt playing it were not when I was fending off its hordes of gimp-masked cultists, but rather when I was nervously looking over my shoulder just in case my wife happened to walk in the room. However, peel back the sordid surface layer and Revival doesn’t have much meat to go along with its many buckets of blood. Heavy-handed storytelling, repeated chase sequences, and uninspired boss encounters meant that no matter how many meatsacks had their skin pierced and flayed by chains that tightened onscreen, Hellraiser: Revival never managed to properly get its hooks into me.

We play as Aiden, a one liner-spouting everyman with some troubling addiction problems who’s on a quest to bring his newly murdered girlfriend back to life the only way he knows how: by making a pact with pale-skinned series poster boy, Pinhead (voiced with trademark unnerving eloquence by original actor Doug Bradley), to slaughter several members of a local death cult and feed their hearts to her partially reanimated remains. It’s a disturbing premise that’s pretty faithful to the first (and best) two films in the Hellraiser series, but I wish its plot was presented in a more dynamic fashion. The exceedingly gory scenes that featured Pinhead and his cenobite pals always had me glued to the screen, but so much of Revival’s roughly nine-hour story is otherwise delivered in drawn-out exposition dumps spouted by secondary characters, and I never really felt too invested beyond the broad strokes. It’s not a great sign when the chatty in-game merchant is doing most of the heavy lifting here, and I’m not just talking about her ammo crates.

Still, at least the shooting is pretty solid, albeit fairly stock standard for the survival horror genre. To be honest, if Revival’s weapon and inventory system borrowed any more from the Resident Evil series you could probably squint and spot a Capcom logo watermarked somewhere onscreen. However, its assortment of upgradeable pistols, shotguns, machine guns, and breakable blades and bats facilitate some fun ways to decapitate and dismember the hedonistic hordes that stand in Aiden’s way, and ammo is scarce enough that I was forced to make use of absolutely everything at my disposal.

I admittedly had to toggle off the overzealous aim assist since it would regularly snap to a single enemy when I was trying to target an explosive barrel in the middle of a group, and I also lamented Aiden’s inability to vault over obstacles. This became particularly ludicrous in one instance where I could clearly see a room full of precious items through a wide open window, but instead of simply jumping through the gap, I had to stop and hunt around for a key to the locked door in order to access them.

Even so, Revival’s mixture of slash-and-sidestep melee encounters and skull-shattering shotgun blasts makes for some gory good times, even if the variety of enemy types is somewhat limited. Beyond the machete and gun-wielding cultists, it’s mostly the same gaggle of gangly ghouls, suicide-bombing beasts, and legless creatures crawling after you that you have to mow down.

There are ample opportunities for stealth, too, with bricks and bottles to throw for distractions and violent stealth kills to pull off. Although I wish there were controls to peek around corners like in the recent Silent Hill: Townfall, because too often I’d be spotted ever-so-slightly stepping out from cover and be forced to go in all-guns-blazing anyway. It was even worse during the occasional instant-fail stealth sections with stalker enemy types, who could sometimes spot me through bushes even when I was standing still.

What elevates Revival’s combat slightly above the norm is the introduction of the Genesis Configuration, a powerful reimagining of the series’ iconic puzzle box that gives Aiden the ability to grab objects like conveniently placed nails and sawblades from his surroundings and hurl them at enemies with forceful blasts of telekinesis. Use of these BioShock-style superpowers is tied to his ‘suffering’ bar, which must be continually topped up by staggering enemies and performing a grisly execution move that jams the hellraising Rubik’s Cube into their mouths and blasts nine inch nails directly into their skulls like they’re front row at Coachella.

I like that the limitations of the suffering bar means these supernatural abilities don’t make you feel too overpowered, and how the short timer on keeping an object suspended in stasis means you can’t confidently wander around with a fanblade ready to launch like you could in Dead Space. Eventually these powers are expanded to let Aiden play with fire, which allowed me to shoot explosive barrels to take out one group of enemies, before hoovering up the resulting flames and hurling them at other monsters hustling over to provide backup. There’s even a bar-draining super move that shackles clusters of creatures together and tears them all apart at the same time, chaining your attacks in a gruesomely literal sense. It’s just a shame that this devastating option for crowd control doesn’t arrive until much later in the story, giving you relatively few opportunities to really put it to use.

It’s also disappointing that Revival’s boss fights are so utterly flat and forgettable for the most part. There are some interesting exceptions like the flying Sister of Mercy, who shrouds the arena in a blood mist and darts at you through the crimson haze, and another beast that scrambles on all fours and locks you in a cage suspended from a tree branch, forcing you to desperately fend off ghouls clumsily climbing up the bars in order to escape and finish the fight. But too many of the boss encounters are boring, close-quarters clashes that barely raise a hair let alone hell, and are just not all that engaging to overcome.

A skinless freak that sluices down into a pool of viscera like some sort of blood-splattered Splatoon character certainly makes one hell of an entrance, but the fight itself demands little in the way of strategy beyond circle-strafing and shooting him until he’s done for. Ditto the second time you face him later on. Meanwhile a sluglike cenobite that has enough arms to give himself a group hug is equally one-note, and you have to fight him a staggering total of four times over the full course of the journey. For all the sharp objects that litter its environments, it's somewhat surprising that Revival’s boss fights can frequently be so dull.

Revival’s puzzles aren’t the sharpest either, typically limited to tried and tested tasks like searching for bolt cutters to bust open chained gates or scouring documents for clues to four-digit keypads. There are at least a handful of occasions where it really leans into its seedier – and at times sillier – side with quandaries that are designed to tease not just your brain but potentially other parts of your anatomy. (No judgement.) At one point I was asked by a latex-clad NPC to go on a treasure hunt for uncomfortable-looking toys in a bondage club in order to progress the story, while at another I found myself flummoxed by a combination lock that demanded I arrange the positions of a variety of couples in an orgy. Truly there are moments where Revival feels a bit like Resident Evil if you swapped out Leon Kennedy for Leisure Suit Larry, and while none of its puzzles are particularly challenging, a number of them are at the very least somewhat unique.

Yet while Revival might be sexually depraved, it’s also disappointingly deprived of any interesting new gameplay ideas elsewhere, regularly cribbing from survival horror classics without doing enough to match them, let alone improve on them. Remember the frantic cabin defense in Resident Evil 4 that saw Leon team up with Luis to board up windows and kick down ladders as crazed villagers spilled in through every entry point? Well, there’s a version of that here set in a much smaller, single-storey space that inspires considerably less in the way of panicked problem solving. How about a looping household hallway a la Hideo Kojima’s P.T.? Yep, that’s in here too, minus any interesting puzzle elements or baby-in-the-sink levels of genuine terror.

Even the absolute fundamentals are regularly fumbled. At one point I powered up an old elevator, and as I waited for it to make its agonisingly slow ascent to my level I steeled myself for a fight, since as we all know nothing spawns enemies faster in a survival horror game than the simple press of a call button. However, as the gun-toting goons inevitably started filing into the room from all corners, I discovered that I could just leave the building through the front door and gun them all down while they funnelled their way through the exit, which completely robbed the moment of its intended intensity.

In occasional departures from the slaughter-filled hallways of sex clubs and cult leader mansions, Aiden is regularly whisked away to the Labyrinth for a brief break from combat. Although this MC Escher-inspired maze of concrete corridors is far more linear than it initially appears, it nonetheless does a great job of capturing the ominous feel of Hellraiser’s infamous realm of torture and pain. From the looming Leviathan on the hellscape’s horizon to the insect-like cenobites that scatter along the walls like grotesquely fleshy cockroaches, it’s initially a very intimidating place to explore. Every jagged surface looks like it could have your eye out, and Revival plays some clever tricks on you to keep you on your toes, like rearranging the walls around you to make you feel like you’re really trapped inside a tangle of impossible architecture.

I very much enjoyed the occasional use of Aiden’s telekinesis power to manipulate large chunks of the environment and create paths through this otherworld, as well as dashing past its spinning instant-deathtraps in order to snare optional upgrades to Aiden’s health and suffering bars. What I did grow tired of, though, were the overused chase sequences that see you pursued by Chatterer, the cenobite from the films that basically resembles a wind-up pair of chattering teeth being smuggled inside a stretched-out skinsuit. The first instance of me being hunted by this rictus-grinning goon certainly may have gotten my blood pumping, but by the third of fourth instance of sliding under the same clusters of chains and obstacles, my heart rate had dipped well below the speed of his perpetually pattering pearly whites.

Still, even though my repeat runs through Revival’s mazes eventually became monotonous, at least they consistently functioned as intended. Back in the story’s mortal realm, things didn’t always seem to go to plan. Beyond minor bugs like enemies glitching through walls and audio dropping out during boss fights that made them seem more silent than violent, there were a handful of more significant errors in the PS5 version I played that, while never completely gamebreaking, were pretty annoying to endure. In one instance, I’d fought my way to a cabin deep in a cemetery and puzzled open a locked safe, only to find that I had no inventory space to claim the gun upgrade inside it. So, I trudged all the way back to the nearest save point to temporarily offload some weapons and ammo into a storage box, only to return to the safe and be frustrated to find it locked again with no button prompt to reopen it.

Later on, I was surprised to find the door to a safehouse had somehow become stuck and wouldn’t budge. It was open wide enough to let me see the merchant calmly blinking back at me, but I couldn’t get close enough to actually buy anything from her. This meant that for about a 30-minute stretch at the more combat-heavy end of the story, I was forced to make do with the scarce amount of ammo I could scrounge from the environment until I finally battled through a number of enemies and a boss fight on my way to the next save point, which made that period substantially more of a grind than it probably should have been.

However, at least I’ll only ever have to suffer these problems once, because although Revival cribs plenty from other, better survival horror series’ like Resident Evil and Silent Hill, one thing it hasn’t replicated is their signature replayability. Although there are two endings to achieve, they each stem from the one binary decision made at the story’s climax, meaning I was able to instantly reload my last save and experience both without having to play through the full story a second time. No matter whether you opt for the thoroughly bleak or more optimistic of the two outcomes, this tale eventually closes with a Pinhead quote that reads, “Your suffering has only just begun, we have such sights to show you.” Apparently those sights don’t include a New Game+ mode or any other form of unlockables, though, because Revival simply boots you out to the main menu with nothing extra to reward you with for completing its story.

articles.title: Hellraiser: Revival Video Review - IGN
articles.summary:
Hellraiser: Revival reviewed by Tristan Ogilvie on PlayStation 5. Also available on Xbox Series X|S, PC, and Nintendo Switch 2.
"As someone who’s been seriously spooked by the Hellraiser movies since I was barely tall enough to reach them on the top shelf of my local video store, I certainly got some thrills from staring down cenobites in Hellraiser: Revival as I stalked the cold, concrete chambers of the sprawling otherworld labyrinth that they call home. Its combat is derivative but solid enough to serve up a satisfying amount of slaughter, and some of the not-safe-for-work (or home) puzzles are certainly memorable, if not particularly challenging. However, Revival often struggles to sustain tension, with enemy encounters that are all too easily manipulated, a story propped up by too much telling and not enough showing, and obnoxiously repeated boss fights and chase sequences that make its nine-hour runtime suffer from more bloat than Butterball’s belly. While the studded scalp of otherworld antagonist Pinhead absolutely looks the part, it’s a shame that little else in Hellraiser: Revival has been nailed to anywhere near the same extent."

articles.title: Xbox Announces New XP Entertainment Division to Make Movies, TV, and More
articles.summary: Xbox has announced a new TV, movies, and entertainment division called XP. It will be headed up by Kayleen Walters, a Lucasfilm veteran who moves over from her most recent post at Minecraft maker Mojang, for whom she was president – and also served as an executive producer on last year's A Minecraft Movie.
articles.body:
Xbox has announced a new TV, movies, and entertainment division called XP. It will be headed up by Kayleen Walters, a Lucasfilm veteran who moves over from her most recent post as president of Minecraft maker Mojang, where she also served as an executive producer on last year's A Minecraft Movie.

XP brings together four "areas of investment": Xbox Pictures; Xbox Products; Xbox Partnerships; and Xbox Places. Microsoft said XP was set up to help Xbox become the number one entertainment and gaming company in the world, which requires broadening its big franchises beyond video games themselves. But it is not a production company. Rather, Microsoft wants to find the right partners to work across film, TV, physical experiences, and consumer products.

Microsoft has already seen significant success in the movie and TV space, with Warner Bros.' A Minecraft Movie breaking box office records, and Amazon's Fallout TV show setting records for Prime Video. Upcoming Xbox adaptations include movie sequel Minecraft Squared, Fallout Season 3, a Call of Duty movie with Peter Berg and Taylor Sheridan, and a Diablo animated series with Netflix . Microsoft's deal for Hideo Kojima's Metal Gear Solid spiritual successor Physint includes film and TV rights, so expect an adaptation of that eventually.

Upcoming New Video Game Movies and TV Shows: 2026 Release Dates and Beyond

XP is also about live events, and again, Xbox already has success there. Blizzard's BlizzCon saw a number of significant announcements , with 35,000 people at the physical event in Anaheim, California, and 12.5 million watching at home. The most recent Minecraft Live , which saw the announcement of the first new dimension for Minecraft in 14 years, reached more than 144 million people.

Meanwhile, Microsoft cited partnerships such as Gears of War's takeover with WWE, and Xbox's range of Ikea furniture . A Minecraft theme park is set to open its gates next year .

"XP was created from a simple but powerful belief: the world's most beloved gaming franchises have an opportunity to reach people far beyond the boundaries of the game itself," Walters said. "Fans don't just play our franchises. They watch them, wear them, attend them, celebrate them, and connect with them in countless ways. XP brings together the teams responsible for helping Xbox franchises show up in the world in bigger, more meaningful ways."

"XP is a play on 'Experience Points' and formalizes four investment areas for us: Xbox Pictures for film and television adaptations; Xbox Products for licensing and merchandise; Xbox Partnerships for sponsors and brand partners; and Xbox Places for our marquee broadcast and in-person events, theme parks, and other location-based experiences," Xbox CEO Asha Sharma wrote in a company-wide memo also posted to Xbox Wire.

"Our franchises can mean more to people than the time they spend playing them, and Kayleen knows how to build those experiences with the industry without losing what made people care about the franchise in the first place."

Microsoft noted the uplift its video games can get when movies and shows do well. For example, Fallout games on Game Pass saw a 5x increase in hours played during Fallout Season 1. Minecraft, meanwhile, saw over a 75% increase in weekly active users year-over-year since the movie released (as of April 30, 2026).

If this sounds a bit familiar, it's because Microsoft has tried this before. In 2012 (back in the Xbox 360 era!), Microsoft announced Xbox Entertainment Studios with an aim to produce TV shows that would air directly on Xbox consoles. XES revealed plans to create shows based on Gears of War, Fable, Forza, and State of Decay — not to mention, of course, the original version of the Halo TV show announced at E3 by Stephen Spielberg , who was set to executive produce. They even planned to make an unscripted street-soccer drama called Every Street United. The entire XES effort lasted just two years before getting shut down as the Xbox One's "all in one" message failed to resonate with gamers following its reveal in 2013.

As part of the changes, Mojang has a new boss. Maria Angelidou-Smith, who joins Xbox as CEO of Mojang, spent nearly a decade at Meta working on Facebook Groups before stints at Personio and Reddit, where she was Chief Product Officer. "She has built products used by billions of people and led product and engineering organizations through significant growth and change," Sharma said.

"She will bring that experience to Mojang while learning from the people who know Minecraft best. Her first order of business is for her to learn from the teams and communities that make Minecraft so special."

Minecraft is, of course, one of the big Xbox franchises the company is doubling down on amid Sharma's ongoing "Reset," which has seen nearly 2,000 staff cut from the gaming business so far this financial year. Minecraft is the best-selling video game of all time, having shifted over 425 million copies. Its significant merchandising business became one of the top 20 globally.

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked , and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch . He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan .

articles.title: Xbox is launching a new film and TV division
articles.summary: Xbox is launching a new division, called “XP,” that’s dedicated to Xbox experiences that aren’t video games themselves, including films and TV adaptations.
articles.body: Xbox is launching a new division, called “XP,” that’s dedicated to Xbox experiences that aren’t video games, including films and TV adaptations, consumer products, live events, and partnerships with creators and brands. Different teams at Xbox already do this work, but it will all now fall under the centralized XP division. XP formalizes four “investment areas,” according to a blog post by Xbox chief strategy officer Matthew Ball: > XBOX PICTURES: Bringing our worlds and characters to new audiences through film, television, and other forms of linear storytelling. > XBOX PRODUCTS: Creating products that are authentic to the fandom that allow fans to celebrate and express the franchises they love. > XBOX PLACES: Bringing communities together through live events, immersive experiences, attractions, broadcasts, and destinations. > XBOX PARTNERSHIPS: Working with creators, brands, and communities to develop new experiences, sponsorships, and brand partnerships. XP will be led by Kayleen Walters, who is moving from her role heading up Minecraft-maker Mojang to be president of the new division. Mojang will next be led by Maria Angelidou-Smith, who is leaving her job as Reddit’s chief product officer to become CEO of Mojang and Minecraft, and she starts on October 19th. Xbox is already developing several film and TV adaptations, including a sequel to the successful A Minecraft Movie, a third season of Prime Video’s Fallout live-action series, a Call of Duty film, and a Diablo animated series for Netflix. “Great games remain at the center of these franchises and at the heart of XBOX,” Ball says. “XP will partner with the best creative minds across our studios, along with trusted partners, to build on that foundation and create more ways for people to experience the worlds they love.” Xbox CEO Asha Sharma also sent an email about the changes to employees. She had previously told staff that the company would build “long-term plans” for Xbox’s franchises “across film, television, consumer products, sponsorship, live experiences” as part of her broader “reset” of the Xbox business. Since taking over in February, Sharma has enacted sweeping layoffs, sold off studios, and made big changes to Xbox’s studio structure, including putting Activision in charge of Halo. In 2012, Microsoft established Xbox Entertainment Studios to make film and TV adaptations of Xbox games, but shut it down two years later.

articles.title: Clive Barker's Hellraiser Revival Review, Gameplay Impressions, Videos and Top Features
articles.summary: Clive Barker's Hellraiser Revival from developer Saber Interactive joins the fray as the genre continues to enjoy a resurgence.
articles.body:
Clive Barker's Hellraiser Revival from developer Saber Interactive joins the fray as the genre continues to enjoy a resurgence.

A first-person survival horror game that brings the iconic IP to next-gen video games, Hellraiser Revival presents a medley of some of the genre's best in the process.

At a time when Resident Evil and a host of others have seized the gaming space, Hellraiser Revival looks less "new kid on the block" and more like a release capable of standing up there with the heavyweights right from the jump.

A Hellraiser game needs to present top-of-line graphical horsepower to accentuate the heaps of gore and violence to really drive home the nail-biting immersive tension.

Hellraiser Revival does just that with all the expected graphical bells and whistles.

This game is not for the faint of heart. Like its source material, there is severe body horror here, full-blown nudity, dismemberment, mutilation and gore.

And yes, on the sound design front, Doug Bradley is back as Pinhead. Just as important, though, are the borderline uncomfortable sound effects that come with the violence.

It's an overall immersive romp, for those seeking it out. The entire vibe is less "time for another jumpscare" and more a persistent unsettling feeling in one's gut.

Combat against humans and other monstrosities hits on the expected stuff in terms of melee and environmental wrinkles. It's responsive and fun. Uncomfortable, given the never-ending tension, but effective at what it sets out to do.

There's an expected, small touch of combat realism in terms of effectiveness. Blunt weapons smash up armor, whereas, from a strategy standpoint, sharp weapons will do more damage to enemies not wearing armor.

As is common in these types of games now, there's a durability system for players to juggle, so finding new weapons is a must.

Not common, though, is the Genesis Configuration. It's a box that bestows users supernatural powers. Think, controlling fire, or ripping sawblades out of a wall to send them ripping through enemies. It's very Bioshock-like, in a good way.

Admittedly, Hellraiser Revival wouldn't be so horrific if it didn't have a brilliant wrinkle: Stealth is mandatory sometimes thanks to the presence of enemies who can't be defeated in combat. Listening for sound cues before ever actually seeing these types of enemies is a nice little survival tip, to say the least.

Beyond combat, players will tackle puzzles, especially of the environmental variety. There's the basic matching and finding stuff, but the Labyrinth puzzles where players mold the path forward are a nice touch.

Crafting via discovered resources is also part of the loop. It's fun enough, and there's just enough ammo scarcity to justify the system and the reliance on things like melee weapons and the little magical cube.

As expected, Clive Barker's fingerprints are all over this.

The tale might land as polarizing for most. Protagonist Aidan Lynch and girlfriend Sunny are split up early on during the intro that is not PG or even PG-13 friendly. The long and the short of it is that Aidan must go through literal hell at times in his efforts to save her from the Cenobites.

Somewhat fittingly, though, Aidan and Sunny are crashouts and biker-gang aligned, so they're not exactly role models or enjoyable. Deacon from Days Gone, these guys are not.

Alas, the story is a vehicle for the gameplay and vice versa. The overall lore ties are fun and any excuse to charge into hell itself works.

Where Hellraiser Revival really shines is in small non-combat sequences inspired by P.T. that feature players taking a lonely nightmare stroll through Aidan's home with some horrifying results and puzzle-like scenarios. It's supernatural horror at its finest and a welcome change of pace from the gory combat.

Hellraiser Revival runs well and comes with the expected suite of options, too.

For those who can stomach body horror and a marriage of sex and violence, Hellraiser Revival is a grotesque movie at a player's fingertips.

In a very basic video game sense, this is almost a film adaptation done right in video game form. The gameplay is solid and the entire package's level of immersion is downright impressive.

Disclaimers aside, Hellraiser Revival is a solid medley of gameplay elements found elsewhere in the space and bathed in a slew of gore. It's not knocking genre heavyweights out of the way, but it is standing on its own as unique.

articles.title: GTA 6 Leaker Returns With New 24-Minute Gameplay Video, Sparking Spoiler Concern
articles.summary: GTA 6 leaker Cyberleek has returned to publish a 24-minute gameplay video that has left fans scrambling to issue spoiler warnings across the internet.
articles.body:
GTA 6 leaker Cyberleek has returned to publish a 24-minute gameplay video that has left fans scrambling to issue spoiler warnings across the internet.

“Cyberleek,” as they are known, uploaded 24 minutes of unauthorized gameplay footage titled “GTA 6: An Extended Leek.” It reportedly contains a number of cutscenes revealing story beats, playable characters Jason and Lucia naked (in the case of Jason, full-frontal nudity), and a first-person camera for driving.

Cyberleek appeared to go dark after a spate of high-profile GTA 6 leaks in August, which sparked an investigation from Rockstar parent company Take-Two that saw subpoenas issued to the likes of Discord. Today's development suggests Cyberleek, whether that's an individual or a group, remains at large. It remains unclear how this gameplay footage, or any potential build of the game it's taken from, escaped the confines of Rockstar's infamous tight security.

In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023

Indeed, at one point in today's leaked video, what looks like a developer menu is used to spawn a tank, which you wouldn't expect would be possible in the launch version of the game. So, it may be the case that Cyberleek has enabled nudity in GTA 6 for this leaked video, but players won't be able to when it comes to actually playing the game.

In August, Rockstar addressed the GTA 6 leaks , describing the situation as "heartbreaking" for its development team and "unfortunate" for fans. At the time, the developer acknowledged that its intended experience for players "may now be impacted by some spoilers," but reiterated GTA 6's previously-confirmed launch date of November 19.

Cyberleek claimed to be leaking material to highlight the death of physical media and the impact this would have on game ownership, while also charging fans to vote on further leaks using cryptocurrency in what was widely-seen as a money-making exercise.

This new gameplay video ends with yet another message that suggests Cyberleek wants more money for some mystery project, but it's hard to parse.

"Cyberleek has a project," the message begins. "Not Rockstar related. Gaming related. It needs expensive hardware. Months to set up. Years to run. Full-time. If you cannot trust the figure, trust the skills. You do not know Cyberleek. Cyberleek could be anyone. Even a liar. That is fair. No blame for doubt. Doubt is the correct default for an unknown. What is collected goes to the project. However much arrives, Cyberleek does the possible with it. That is the only promise."

Cyberleek was heavily criticized for using GTA 6 leaks to push a meme coin. Analysis of cryptocurrency transactions in late August pointed to the GTA 6 leaker having "cashed out," earning around $270,000 in the process. Every video posted by Cyberleek pointed to a website where fans could pay to vote on further leaks using the leaker's own cryptocurrency.

articles.title: Hands-on with Amazon’s Alexa Tablet 12 Pro and its wild new matte display
articles.summary: Amazon’s Alexa Tablet 12 Pro runs full Android, has Google Play access, and features a Nanomatte screen that shrugs off bright, glaring sunlight at any angle.
articles.body: Amazon’s Fire tablets are notable for being dirt cheap. While they’re great for kids, they don’t offer a premium Android tablet experience. The company’s new $499 Alexa Tablet 12 Pro is an attempt to build a device someone might actually want to use. It’s one of a few new Android tablets Amazon announced today, and it’s the one you need to know about. Unlike the Fire Tablet lineup, the Alexa Tablet doesn’t run some hobbled version of Android stuck with Amazon’s app store with ads for Amazon services at every turn. It has full access to the Google Play app store. It’s powered by 8GB or 12GB of RAM with a MediaTek Dimensity 8400 8-core CPU. That’s more than enough for light gaming, powering Alexa, and running basic apps, but don’t expect Alien: Isolation to run super smoothly. The aluminum unibody feels great. It’s light at 550 grams (1.2 pounds), but not flimsy. It’s slightly lighter than the 13-inch iPad Air (617 grams) but heavier than the 11-inch (465 grams). The screen is the truly exciting thing about the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro. The $549.99 Alexa Tablet 12 Pro has a 12.3-inch 3:2 display that can be configured with Corning’s Nanomatte tech, similar to Apple’s nano-texture, which reduces glare and gives the screen a more paper-like feel. [Image: The difference between the Nanomatte display and the standard glossy one is dramatic. It’s impossible to do it justice in photos or video. The Nanomatte coating doesn’t simply reduce glare; it almost completely eliminates it. Amazon held a briefing in a brightly sunlit room, and I thought the 12 Pro was a dummy unit when I first saw it. It looked like a cardboard placeholder image was placed inside. Then an Amazon rep started swiping around the screen. There’s also a standard glossy option, and the difference is shocking. In the bright sunlight of the room, the glossy screen was basically a mirror and was easily washed out when viewed at an angle. The Nanomatte display, however, was clearly readable at any angle and barely reflected any ambient light. Only at extreme angles in the brightest patches of light did it become difficult to see. The screen pairs particularly well with the immersive Kindle mode. Here, background activities are limited, notifications are silenced, and blue light is lowered to reduce eye strain. There are three different Kindle-specific display modes. Standard delivers the full vibrancy of the screen; Color offers a softer, more muted experience; and Ink is full grayscale. In Kindle mode, battery life is also extended from 16 hours to 20 hours. [Media: Without having the two side-by-side, it’s hard to say how it compares to Apple’s matte display on the iPad Pro, but anecdotally it seems to retain slightly more contrast. Using a stylus with it is much more pleasant than on a glossy display, but I can’t say I noticed a difference between it and an iPad. The Alexa Tablet Pro Pen and Pro Keyboard attach magnetically and seem serviceable enough. I wouldn’t want to type on its shallow, cramped keys all day, but they’re fine for knocking out a few emails. The keyboard case was a little clunky to get on and off, though. It’s actually two parts — the back cover and stand are separate from the keyboard base. Alexa Everywhere [Image: Go ahead, ask Alexa. I dare you. I double dare you. The tablet shoves Alexa down your throat at every turn. In the bottom right-hand corner is an “Ask Alexa” bar that lets you quickly chat with the AI assistant. And in the top left-hand corner is what Amazon calls the Dynamic Tab. It offers up proactive suggestions from Alexa. That can be something as simple as picking up where you left off in a book or movie, or offering an itinerary for a three-day trip to New York. This is, of course, powered by Amazon’s deep well of information it gathers from your reading, viewing, and shopping habits. Amazon keeps some of Alexa’s more invasive features off by default. On-Screen Intelligence, which can see what you’re doing and take actions based on what’s actually on your screen, is strictly opt-in. There are also robust controls for limiting what Alexa can hear and remember. If you do opt in, though, Alexa becomes a pretty powerful shopping companion. I was able to open random photos from the internet and ask Alexa to find me something in them, like a coffee table or a mirror, and, even if it couldn’t track down the exact thing, it found something close. Then it would add it to my Amazon cart if I asked. How likely am I to ask Alexa to track down a bathroom fixture for me from a Pinterest photo and deliver it to my house in two days via Prime? Not very. I’m also unlikely to have it automatically add school holidays to my calendar from the Department of Education site, but it will if you ask it to. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: The Alexa Tablet 12 Pro starts at $499.99, but you’ll have to shell out at least $549.99 for the Nanomatte model. If you want to tack on the keyboard case and the Pro Pen, that will be an additional $149.99 and $89.99, respectively. Amazon also announced two smaller models that lack the Nanomatte screen options. The Alexa Tablet 11 starts at $329.99, while the Alexa Tablet 8 starts at $229.99. Those come in more fun colorways, including rosette and matcha, in addition to the drab but functional graphite of the Tablet 12 Pro.

articles.title: GTA VI leaks continue with a lengthy (and very nude) gameplay video
articles.summary: A new 25-minute video of GTA 6 footage from leaker Cyberleek reportedly shows the game’s main characters naked, with light story spoilers.
articles.body: The GTA VI leaks keep coming — and the latest is almost as long as the game’s official “extended look” on Netflix. Only instead of showing off all the various gameplay details, this one is more of an “extended look” at Jason running around Vice City naked. As Kotaku reports, GTA leaker Cyberleek, who cashed out on a memecoin and seemingly disappeared earlier this year, is back with a new 25-minute video of GTA VI gameplay. The video suggests players will be able to play through GTA VI with their characters completely unclothed. According to Kotaku, Jason is naked throughout almost the whole video, including while on a motorbike, “at a beach-side coffee store,” and while talking to other characters. Lucia is also mostly naked in a clip at the end of the video, where Cyberleek reportedly briefly shows her from behind. Some of the leaked footage appears to include light story spoilers, with Kotaku noting that the video opens with a cutscene of Jason and Lucia leading into a dirt bike race for one of the game’s scripted missions. Cyberleek goes on to show some first-person driving footage from Jason, followed by a street race. Kotaku also says Cyberleek “seemingly conjures a tank out of the air” and, of course, uses the video to advertise a crypto coin. Cyberleek previously shared a slew of other GTA VI clips in the lead up to the game’s Netflix special. Rockstar Games eventually responded, calling the leaks “heartbreaking,” and Take-Two has requested multiple subpoenas as it tries to find the “alleged infringers” leaking the game footage. Before that, a massive collection of videos leaked in 2022, and the hacker was eventually sentenced to life in hospital prison. Grand Theft Auto VI is available for preorder now and set to launch on November 19th.

articles.title: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered Patch Adds Bloom Toggles on Console and Larger Lighting Changes
articles.summary: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered just got a significant update to tweak the presentation of CD Projekt’s RPG epic. Check out the patch notes.
articles.body:
The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered just got a significant patch to tweak the presentation of CD Projekt’s RPG epic.

Despite the remaster offering a host of improvements over the base game — visually and mechanically — not everyone was happy with how it turned out. Some fans across Reddit and social media complained about its heavy bloom effects, which created a washed out look and removed many of the original game’s stark shadows. Tonally, it felt meaningfully different, and the overdone bloom made it difficult to appreciate other graphical improvements.

“I started the training part at the beginning of the game [and] I noticed that the blooming effects are jacked all the way up which causes the image to look washed out and makes everything look too bright in the environment,” one Reddit poster said. “At first I assumed that it was either the game or my TV settings but after messing with the settings for like an hour I realized that it's actually the game having a ridiculous blooming effect. The PC version allows people to shut the blooming off but the console version doesn't have a way to turn off the blooming.”

The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered Screenshots

The latest patch addresses that issue, allowing console players to toggle bloom off, along with light shafts, and depth of field. Elsewhere, the developer has made improvements to bloom, tone mapping, character lighting, and fancy ray tracing and path tracing tech.

“In addition to this, we are also working on an update for the Nintendo Switch 2 version of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered, introducing closer parity between all versions of the game, including the same global changes as on other platforms,” CD Projekt said in the blog post. “It will also improve on some Nintendo Switch 2-specific aspects, such as image clarity and sharpness. Expect more information regarding this in the following days.”

Prior to the latest patch, fans were creating Steam Forum threads urging other players to switch bloom off entirely. In one comparison shot , you can see how bloom impacted the overall image before the improvements.

Patch 5.01 is roughly 5.5 GB on console and 8.5 GB on PC. There’s no word yet on whether The Witcher 3’s remaster will make use of QSSR, Sony’s new upscaling method for base PS5 . CD Projekt has typically been at the forefront of tech advances, with its previous game, Cyberpunk 2077 , still an absolute showcase of what a good gaming PC can do.

CD Projekt’s next major game will be The Witcher 4 , part continuation part reboot, where you play as Geralt’s adopted daughter, Ciri, as she learns to carry the burden of a Witcher. It’s still a while off, however, with The Witcher 4 planned for a 2028 release .

Before that, in 2027, we’ll get a brand new expansion for The Witcher 3, called Songs of the Past . The new expansion will be as big and ambitious as Blood & Wine, working as a gap filler between the events of The Witcher 3 and its sequel.

To ease you into Geralt’s life on the road, check out the Things The Witcher 3 Doesn’t Tell You , plus IGN’s The Witcher 3 Walkthrough and The Witcher 3 Endings guide, which outlines all of the major quests and choices in the base game and expansions (now bundled in with the Remastered edition). When you’re ready for the tough choices, check out our The Witcher 3 Sex and Romance guide to see who Geralt can smooch and all the opportunities to do so. And to make Geralt as strong a monster hunter as possible, check out all the Witcher Gear Locations , Places of Power Locations , and even Gwent Card Locations .

The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered update 5.01 patch notes:

Fixed an issue where the "Automatically Apply Blade Oils" feature would work only if enabled during the current game session.

Fixed an issue where, under specific circumstances, player-controlled boats could start moving uncontrollably and ignore terrain collisions.

Fixed an issue where Geralt would collide with dead enemies after the Aard finisher.

Fixed an issue where Vesemir would repeatedly say the same line if Quen was cast multiple times.

Fixed an issue where dodging could have an unintentionally delayed response.

Fixed an issue where it was possible to throw a bomb even if the option is disabled.

Fixed an issue where the bonus granted by the Synergy skill displayed incorrect values.

Added damage reflection to the Exploding Shield skill.

Fixed an issue where Geralt's Stamina would be fully drained when sprinting and dodging at the same time.

Fixed an issue where the "You've gained an ability point!" pop-up could stay stuck on the screen.

Fixed input hints flashing for a brief moment on the meditation screen.

Fixed an issue where the Potions tutorial didn't appear after accessing the Consumables tab.

Fixed some misaligned progress bars in the UI.

Fixed an issue where the GTAO Quality setting would reset after restarting the game.

Fixed an issue where Dynamic Resolution Scaling could display the wrong setting after changing the Anti-Aliasing mode.

Fixed cases in which it was possible to enable a graphics setting when using a GPU that doesn't support it.

Fixed an issue where switching graphics presets could apply DLSS or XeSS on GPUs where they're not supported.

Changed the default Dynamic Resolution Scaling setting to OFF.

Fixed an issue where Skill tooltips wouldn't update until hovered over again.

Fixed an issue where the game could sometimes select the wrong GPU.

Added Bloom, Light Shafts, and Depth of Field options to the graphics settings.

Made various optimizations to improve performance.

Fixed an issue where settings on PlayStation 5 would reset every time the game was launched.

The fix for voiceover audio becoming significantly quieter than other in-game audio after navigating through the pause menu tabs is now also implemented on consoles.

Fixed issues with incorrect frame rate limits in different graphics modes on the base PlayStation 5.

Ukrainian text localization is now available in all regions.

Made various visual adjustments, including improvements to Bloom, tone mapping, character lighting, Ray Tracing, and Path Tracing.

Due to backend issues, the policy consent screen will appear again. You’ll need to confirm your preferences once more. Choosing to opt in helps us improve the game.

Fixed an issue where My Rewards and Twitch/Bilibili Drops wouldn't appear in the chest in Vizima if it had been opened previously. As a result of this fix, some of the items may be duplicated. Consider them a bonus!

Fixed an issue where foliage did not react to collisions.

Fixed an issue that could affect save file data and added measures to address saves that may have already been affected.

Fixed an issue where Dynamic Resolution Scaling could cause visual artifacts in certain configurations.
